Notes: Helps international and other new taught postgraduates navigate without needing to understand building conventions.
Section: 6. Part-time, commuting and international-student routines
Sensors_Required: No environmental sensor is required for naming or basic wayfinding. Optional authorised lift, entrance, door and closure status can make the route current; aggregate footfall may support a broad congestion estimate. Use a verified current topology and time-stamped operational status. Use current official status and instrumented route segments; an unobserved segment remains unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: current room and floor naming, public/student route graph, destination, access permissions, open entrances, lift and closure status, verified landmarks and plain-language accessibility information. The May 2021 drawing is a historical aid only.
Analysis_Required: Authoritative lookup + plain-language route generation: resolve the current destination, floor, entrance and permitted route; translate verified room/floor identifiers into clear landmarks and turn-by-turn instructions; include lift or step-free details only when current status is known.
Answer_Boundary: Do not rely on a historic room label or invent landmarks. Route guidance must respect access restrictions and temporary closures. If the destination or current route graph is ambiguous, ask for clarification or direct the student to official signage/reception.

Question: I would rather walk a little farther than use a very crowded corridor. Which open route should I take now?
Notes: Supports confidence and orientation for students who are unfamiliar with the building or prefer lower-crowding routes.
Section: 6. Part-time, commuting and international-student routines
Sensors_Required: Required evidence: privacy-preserving aggregate corridor/stair footfall and doorway counts at relevant route segments; current lift, door and closure status. Use verified route mapping, aligned timestamps, known counter coverage and no identity or personal-device tracking. Use current official status and instrumented route segments; an unobserved segment remains unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: destination and current authorised route graph, access permissions, temporary closures, step-free requirement if any, and the student's stated willingness to trade distance for lower crowding.
Analysis_Required: Current estimate and recommendation: estimate segment congestion from recent counts, calculate travel time for feasible routes and rank the Pareto trade-off between distance and crowding; provide a fallback and recheck time around class change.
Answer_Boundary: An uninstrumented segment is unknown, not empty. Counts may be inaccurate at multi-entry junctions and do not identify people. Never route through restricted areas; if coverage is insufficient, provide the shortest verified route without a crowding claim.

Question: Where can I join a 30-minute online call before my evening class, while still being able to reach the class and leave the building afterwards?
Notes: Supports a common pattern for part-time students balancing work calls and evening teaching.
Section: 6. Part-time, commuting and international-student routines
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry: numerical LAeq/L10/L90 inside candidate rooms, anonymous occupancy, authorised network-service health, room/circuit power status and door state; optional room temperature/NDIR CO2 for a longer wait. Record no speech and use current sensor/service-quality metadata. Require verified room mapping, synchronised timestamps, health and gap flags; corridor data is contextual and network evidence remains aggregate.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: rooms currently authorised for student online calls, booking or drop-in rules, opening and exit times, next-class room and access route, network incidents, capacity and accessibility. The May 2021 plan does not establish present call suitability.
Analysis_Required: Lookup plus recommendation: filter to authorised call-suitable spaces available for the full interval and a viable route to class; classify network/power status; compare aggregate sound and occupancy; rank a primary and backup and state the latest departure time.
Answer_Boundary: Low background sound does not guarantee conversational privacy or speech intelligibility. The system must not listen to the call or guarantee the external meeting platform. If no enclosed or appropriately designated space is verified, say so and provide the official alternative.

Question: Is it worth travelling to Abacws for an optional study day tomorrow? What study spaces, services and likely conditions are available, so I can compare them with working remotely?
Notes: Helps a commuter make a transparent choice about an optional campus visit.
Section: 6. Part-time, commuting and international-student routines
Sensors_Required: For Abacws only: proposed room-level anonymous occupancy, numerical sound, air temperature/relative humidity, direct NDIR CO2 and task illuminance; authorised network and room/circuit power status. Use verified in-room mapping, source timestamps, health, coverage and missing-data flags. Require verified room mapping, synchronised timestamps, health and gap flags; corridor data is contextual and network evidence remains aggregate.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: actual PGT-accessible spaces, bookings, opening hours, network/power incidents, timetable, route and weather. Remote-study conditions, travel burden and personal preferences are used only when the student explicitly supplies them for this comparison.
Analysis_Required: Decision support: verify tomorrow's opening, access, bookings and service status; forecast candidate-space crowding and measured conditions; compare only with the remote-study criteria the student chooses to provide; present trade-offs rather than a single prescriptive answer.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer home conditions, costs, caring duties, disability or attendance obligations. The system cannot decide whether travel is personally worthwhile. If campus or remote evidence is incomplete, show the unknowns and leave the decision to the student.

Question: Can I opt in to an alert if a room change, lift problem, entrance closure, network incident or other confirmed service issue affects my planned visit?
Notes: Gives part-time and commuting students time to adjust before travelling.
Section: 6. Part-time, commuting and international-student routines
Sensors_Required: No continuous personal sensing is required. Use only authorised event feeds for official room changes, lift/entrance closures, access-service incidents, network or power outages and, where configured, room-level environmental alerts. Require source identity, event time, severity, expiry and service-health metadata. Use current official route and aggregate service status; unobserved segments remain unknown and no content, credentials or identifiable traffic may be inspected.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: an opt-in visit plan with the minimum times/locations needed, official timetable and room-change notifications, building and IT incidents, notification preferences, consent, expiry and revocation state.
Analysis_Required: Event matching + opt-in notification: monitor only the submitted visit window and authorised dependencies; deduplicate and prioritise official events; determine whether each event affects the planned location/time; send the source, timestamp, expected impact, official action and expiry.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer attendance, continuously track the student or retain the visit plan beyond its purpose. Notifications are advisory and may be delayed; official course and emergency communications take precedence. The student must be able to pause, amend and revoke the service.

Question: What is the best step-free route to my seminar if I also prefer lower crowding and lower background noise?
Notes: Supports a more usable route for taught postgraduates with mobility or sensory preferences.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required operational evidence: current lift, entrance, accessible-door and closure state; privacy-preserving aggregate corridor/stair footfall; numerical sound statistics only on route segments where correctly deployed. Verify every route segment, source timestamp and coverage; record no speech or identity. Require verified room and route mapping, synchronised timestamps, health and gap flags; corridor data is contextual and unobserved route segments remain unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: verified step-free route graph, destination, current access permissions and closures, lift service state, official accessibility assistance route and only the mobility or low-stimulation preferences the student chooses to provide.
Analysis_Required: Accessible route recommendation: first remove every route that fails the declared access requirement; then estimate current crowding and broad sound conditions on remaining routes; rank by the student's priorities and provide a verified fallback and recheck time.
Answer_Boundary: Accessibility is a hard constraint, not a weighted preference. Do not infer disability, retain sensitive needs unnecessarily or expose them to others. If any required lift, door or route segment is unverified, do not label the route step-free; provide the official assistance contact.

Question: Is the lift I need working now, and what step-free alternative should I use if it is not?
Notes: Prevents a student from relying on an inaccessible route and gives a clear fallback.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required operational evidence: authorised lift-controller run/fault state, maintenance outage status and relevant entrance/door/closure state; optional aggregate route footfall. Environmental or movement sensors cannot establish lift availability. Use current source timestamps and service health. Use current official status and instrumented route segments; an unobserved segment remains unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: current accessible-route graph, destination, lift service and maintenance system, temporary closures, building support contact and any authorised assistance procedure.
Analysis_Required: Authoritative lookup plus fallback routing: report the lift state, source and timestamp; calculate only routes whose every step-free segment is verified; if no route remains, state that clearly and present the official assistance process.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer lift operation from door noise, movement or past reliability. A stale controller feed is unknown, not available. Official signage and staff instructions override the chatbot, especially during an incident.

Question: Which accessible student space is likely to be quieter and less crowded, with steady lighting and reasonable temperature and ventilation indicators?
Notes: Helps a student choose a setting that better supports focused postgraduate work.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry (proposed unless verified): correctly located in-room numerical sound, task illuminance/flicker where relevant, air temperature/relative humidity, direct NDIR CO2 and anonymous aggregate occupancy; door state and broad route footfall for access context. Use calibrated/commissioned points, current health, room mapping and missingness; no speech recording.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: present PGT-accessible spaces and permitted use, booking/drop-in status, opening hours, verified step-free routes and lift state, current closures and the student's stated low-noise, low-crowding or lighting preferences.
Analysis_Required: Current observation + recommendation: filter spaces by verified access and any declared accessibility needs; compare numerical sound, aggregate occupancy, lighting stability, temperature and CO2 using correctly located points; rank a primary and backup and state which criteria are unmeasured.
Answer_Boundary: This is a low-stimulation space recommendation, not a medical or sensory-needs assessment. Do not infer disability or retain preferences unnecessarily. Sound level does not prove privacy or absence of sudden events; invalid room-level coverage requires a limited or no recommendation.

Question: I have two intensive sessions back to back. Where can I take a ten-minute quiet break without making the next room difficult to reach?
Notes: Builds a practical recovery period into an intensive taught-postgraduate day.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required evidence: numerical sound and anonymous aggregate occupancy in verified break areas, current corridor footfall and optional room temperature/CO2; lift and door status for the onward route. Use current, correctly mapped sources with explicit gaps and no speech or identity capture. Require verified room and route mapping, synchronised timestamps, health and gap flags; corridor data is contextual and unobserved route segments remain unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: next-session room/time supplied by the student, current PGT-accessible break areas, permitted use, opening, route and closure status, and any step-free requirement.
Analysis_Required: Short-gap recommendation: calculate the usable break duration after walking and buffer time; filter to authorised spaces; compare current sound/crowding and route reliability; rank a nearby option and tell the student when to leave.
Answer_Boundary: This is not a health or rest prescription and cannot guarantee a seat or silence. Do not recommend staff-only or unverified spaces. If route or access status is uncertain, prioritise reaching the next session over environmental preference.

Question: This room feels warm and stuffy. Are the room-level measurements unusual, and what nearby student space could I use for the rest of my study session?
Notes: Gives the student a proportionate, evidence-based option rather than a vague complaint.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry (proposed unless verified): correctly located in-room air temperature/relative humidity and direct NDIR CO2; PM2.5 and indicative TVOC only where installed and quality-controlled; anonymous occupancy and serving-zone airflow/fan state; comparable data for authorised alternatives. Use current room/HVAC mapping and explicit missingness.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: present room use and access, booking, duration remaining, verified nearby PGT alternatives, route/closure status, facilities reporting process and any operational bands selected by the institution.
Analysis_Required: Observation, contextual comparison and recommendation: report current values and rate of change; compare with the room baseline and alternatives over the same window; estimate whether conditions are likely to persist; recommend stay, move or report with reasons and uncertainty.
Answer_Boundary: Perceived warmth or stuffiness is not a diagnosis. CO2 is only a ventilation indicator, and TVOC is not compound-specific. Without valid in-room evidence or an available alternative, provide the reporting route rather than recommend a move. Withhold causal judgement when periods or coverage are not comparable.

Question: Is this study area likely to develop distracting glare later this afternoon, and which alternative has a lower predicted risk?
Notes: Helps a student avoid an interruption during screen-intensive reading or analysis.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry (proposed unless verified): task-plane and, where possible, eye-level illuminance or luminance proxy at representative positions, solar irradiance, blind state, room orientation and cloud/weather input; anonymous occupancy for candidate availability context. Use commissioned placement, aligned time and coverage metadata.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: present PGT-accessible spaces, current furniture/display orientation, blind operability, bookings, opening hours, route and closure status. The May 2021 layout is not evidence of current desk positions or blinds.
Analysis_Required: Forecast and recommendation: model afternoon solar position and weather, combine it with measured daylight/blind histories, estimate glare-risk windows at representative positions and rank authorised alternatives with prediction intervals and a recheck time.
Answer_Boundary: Illuminance alone cannot determine all glare or individual visual comfort, and a room-level forecast cannot guarantee a particular seat. Without eye-level/orientation or blind information, report daylight trend only and mark glare comparison not assessable.

Question: Which open route is likely to avoid the busiest stairs during the next class change?
Notes: Helps a student move reliably between tightly spaced postgraduate sessions.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required evidence: privacy-preserving aggregate counts on relevant stairs, corridors and doors; current lift/door/closure status for alternative routes. Verify segment mapping, timestamp, counter health and coverage; do not use identifiable device tracking. Use current official status and instrumented route segments; an unobserved segment remains unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: current authorised route graph, destination and arrival deadline, access permissions, class-change timetable, temporary closures and any step-free requirement supplied by the student.
Analysis_Required: Near-term forecast and route recommendation: forecast segment demand over the next class change from current counts and scheduled releases; remove inaccessible/restricted routes; compare travel-time distributions and recommend a route with an alternative and refresh point.
Answer_Boundary: Counts at multi-entry junctions may be uncertain, and an uninstrumented stair is unknown rather than quiet. Do not compromise a step-free requirement or route through restricted areas to reduce crowding.

Question: I have a temporary mobility limitation. Which suitable room and step-free route would make our group meeting least likely to be disrupted?
Notes: Makes group-work planning more inclusive during a temporary change in mobility.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required evidence: authorised lift, entrance and accessible-door status; privacy-preserving route footfall; anonymous room occupancy and room-condition telemetry only for verified candidate rooms. Use current topology, source timestamps and coverage; no personal tracking. Use current official status and instrumented route segments; an unobserved segment remains unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: the temporary access requirement the student chooses to state, current step-free route graph, room access/bookability, capacity, group requirements, closures, assistance contact and an authorised backup room.
Analysis_Required: Accessible room and route recommendation: treat every stated access requirement as a hard filter; verify route and room; estimate disruption risk from current service state and recent reliability; then rank valid rooms and supply a contingency.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer the nature or duration of the limitation or share it without consent. An empty room is not necessarily bookable, and any route with an unverified lift or door cannot be called accessible. If no valid option exists, give the official assistance route.

Question: Why can you not currently tell me whether this room is comfortable or has good air quality?
Notes: Builds trust by making the limits of the talking building visible rather than hiding them behind fluent language.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Required evidence is the observability metadata itself: installed/proposed sensor type, exact room or served-zone mapping, measurement method, unit, calibration/commissioning, latest timestamp, uptime, missingness and spatial coverage; relevant non-sensor context such as occupancy and HVAC may also be required. Use time-stamped, health-checked sources with explicit provenance and missing-data flags.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: present room use, access and geometry, serving-HVAC relationship, sensor inventory and maintenance, data-quality records, selected comfort or air-quality definition and any user preference voluntarily supplied. The historic plan cannot establish current instrumentation or use.
Analysis_Required: Answerability explanation: map 'comfortable' and 'good air quality' to the environmental and personal factors required; list which variables, room coverage, calibration, time window and authoritative context are available; distinguish what can be observed from what remains not assessable.
Answer_Boundary: Do not convert a partial temperature/CO2 reading into a comfort, health or compliance judgement. Personal thermal comfort also depends on radiant temperature, air speed, activity, clothing and individual preference; air quality may require PM, VOC or other context. Missing evidence must remain explicit.

Question: There is an alarm or possible emergency. What official instruction should I follow, and where can I find authoritative route information?
Notes: Provides a clear boundary for the highest-consequence interaction a student may attempt.
Section: 7. Accessibility, well-being, navigation and live conditions
Sensors_Required: Use only authorised certified alarm/incident-system status and official lift, door or route closures released for occupants. Experimental environmental, acoustic or occupancy sensing is not the primary emergency source and must not be used to infer an all-clear. Use current official status and instrumented route segments; an unobserved segment remains unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: official alarm state and message, evacuation or shelter instruction, building signage/status, University security or emergency contact and any incident-specific authorised route information.
Analysis_Required: Authoritative emergency lookup: display the latest official instruction, source and timestamp; direct the student to follow alarms, signage, staff and emergency services; provide a route only when the authorised emergency system supplies one.
Answer_Boundary: Do not diagnose the incident, delay evacuation, override an alarm, declare an area safe or improvise a route from ordinary sensor data. If the official feed is unavailable, instruct the student to follow on-site alarms and staff and contact emergency services as appropriate.

Question: For our four-person project meeting, which room is the right size and likely to avoid unnecessary energy use without giving us poorer measured conditions?
Notes: Lets students make a practical sustainability choice without sacrificing a usable working environment.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Design requirement: anonymous occupancy; in-room temperature/RH and direct NDIR CO2; lighting and HVAC state; room-, zone- or system-level electricity/heat metering with current topology. Use aligned, quality-flagged intervals, exclude unresolved gaps and make shared-load allocation explicit.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: current four-person-appropriate rooms, access and booking, capacity and permitted use, meeting duration, accessibility, required services, HVAC/meter relationships and operating rules. The May 2021 plan is not evidence of current room or meter topology.
Analysis_Required: Multi-criteria recommendation + bounded energy calculation: apply access, booking, capacity, activity and accessibility first; estimate marginal or allocated energy only where meter/HVAC topology supports it; compare measured-condition risk; rank options and show shared loads and uncertainty.
Answer_Boundary: A smaller, empty-looking or warmer room is not automatically lower energy. Shared HVAC and baseloads may prevent room attribution. Never trade away access, safety or required service for energy savings; if metering is inadequate, omit the energy criterion.

Question: During deadline week, which empty areas appear to be lit, heated, cooled or ventilated when they may not need to be?
Notes: Gives a taught postgraduate a defensible sustainability-project question that links occupancy, controls and energy without labelling every after-hours operation as waste.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required (proposed unless verified): anonymous aggregate occupancy; lighting state and illuminance; HVAC fan/airflow, valve/damper and zone call; room/zone temperature; electricity or heat metering with verified serving topology. Use synchronised, quality-flagged streams and documented operating schedules; do not identify occupants.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: student-project data permission, verified monitored spaces, current room use, booking/timetable, opening and cleaning/maintenance schedules, HVAC/lighting control intent, meter topology and exclusions for safety, fabric protection or required ventilation.
Analysis_Required: Historical exception analysis: identify periods with high-confidence vacancy; compare observed lighting/HVAC operation with authorised schedules and control requirements; calculate duration and, only where metering supports it, associated energy; rank candidate cases for investigation.
Answer_Boundary: Vacancy estimates and control state do not prove waste. Exclude mandatory ventilation, frost protection, cleaning, maintenance and sensor uncertainty. Do not expose room-use patterns at a level that creates privacy or security risk; report 'not attributable' when meter topology is inadequate.

Question: After the ventilation controls were changed, did energy use fall without worsening CO2 or temperature during similar classes?
Notes: Supports a rigorous taught-postgraduate building-performance assignment rather than a superficial dashboard comparison.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry: room temperature and NDIR CO2, anonymous occupancy, serving-zone airflow/fan/damper/valve state, and electricity/heat metering with verified topology; outdoor weather. Preserve intervention date, control version, calibration/commissioning, gaps and topology changes. Require verified room and meter topology, aligned timestamps, health and gap flags; corridor data is contextual and shared loads must be explicit.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: approved project access, intervention specification and date, affected rooms/equipment, comparable class timetable and expected attendance, maintenance/override records, operating targets and any control spaces.
Analysis_Required: Intervention evaluation: select comparable pre/post sessions and, where possible, unaffected control rooms; normalise for occupancy, weather and schedule; estimate changes in energy, CO2 and temperature with uncertainty; test whether gains persist and report trade-offs.
Answer_Boundary: A simple before/after average cannot establish the intervention effect. Do not claim causality when controls, occupancy, weather, metering or room use changed simultaneously. Apply data permissions and return a limited result when no credible comparison exists.

Question: Roughly how much building energy can reasonably be associated with our late-evening study session compared with a similar daytime session?
Notes: Teaches students how to make a transparent energy-attribution estimate without overstating what building meters can resolve.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry: room/zone electricity and, where relevant, thermal-energy meters; HVAC, lighting and plug-load state; anonymous occupancy; outdoor weather. Use verified meter boundaries, allocation topology, clock alignment and missing-data flags. Require current meter topology, aligned intervals and explicit treatment of shared loads and gaps.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: project permission, session room/time/duration, current room use, operating schedules, comparable daytime sessions, tariff/carbon factors only if required, and exclusions for shared or mandatory loads.
Analysis_Required: Bounded calculation: construct a counterfactual from comparable occupied and unoccupied periods; separate measured, allocated and modelled loads; estimate an energy range attributable to the session and show shared baseload/HVAC uncertainty.
Answer_Boundary: Do not present whole-floor or shared HVAC consumption as the group's exact energy use. Avoid named attendance data and moral judgements. If submetering or allocation topology is inadequate, report the directly measured zone/building change and mark session attribution not assessable.

Question: I have found a leak, overflowing waste point or damaged fitting. What is the official reporting route, and can I see a privacy-safe acknowledgement status?
Notes: Makes it easier for students to report sustainability and maintenance problems and know that they entered the correct process.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required evidence may include a time-stamped point/cable leak detector, water-flow anomaly, bin-fill or local equipment fault where deployed, but the student report and authorised maintenance workflow remain primary. Use current sensor health, exact location mapping and event provenance; no camera or identity is required by default.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: current room/location naming and access, official facilities or waste reporting channel, incident category, priority and safety instructions, work-order acknowledgement state and permission rules for what status may be shown to the reporter.
Analysis_Required: Authoritative issue reporting + status lookup: classify the reported location and issue, attach only necessary evidence, submit through the official channel, return a case reference, and expose only permitted acknowledgement states such as received, assigned or closed.
Answer_Boundary: Do not publish the reporter's identity, other users' reports, security-sensitive detail or maintenance notes. For an immediate hazard, leak near electricity or emergency condition, direct the student to on-site staff/security/emergency procedures rather than waiting for the catalogue service.

Question: The room display and the talking-building answer show different temperature or CO2 values. Which one should I rely on, and how will the conflict be resolved?
Notes: Helps students understand why building data can disagree and prevents false precision.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required evidence: both displayed and queried source identifiers, exact observed property, unit, room/zone mapping, sampling and display aggregation, latest raw timestamp, calibration/commissioning, health, missingness and any transformation or rounding. Preserve independent provenance for each value. Use time-stamped, health-checked sources with explicit provenance and missing-data flags.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: current sensor/display configuration, unit and timezone, data pipeline and cache status, maintenance or replacement history, room mapping and the official source-of-truth policy for that service.
Analysis_Required: Conflict diagnosis: compare source identity, sensor location, observed property, unit, timestamp, averaging window, calibration/commissioning and transformation logic; determine whether the values are genuinely inconsistent, differently aggregated or stale; select the authoritative display source where policy defines one.
Answer_Boundary: Do not choose the numerically convenient value or hide disagreement. A corridor sensor and in-room point are not interchangeable. If source metadata or calibration is insufficient, report the conflict unresolved and direct it to the data owner.

Question: How confident is this room recommendation, which evidence is weakest, and when should I recheck it?
Notes: Lets a postgraduate decide whether to rely on the answer for a high-value study or assessed activity.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required evidence is the complete provenance bundle for the recommendation: source IDs, room/route mapping, units, timestamps, calibration or service health, uptime, missingness, spatial coverage and forecast model/version for every criterion used. Use time-stamped, health-checked sources with explicit provenance and missing-data flags.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: candidate access/bookability, current service states, requested constraints, comparison history, model validation results, permission rules and the time at which the recommendation expires or must be refreshed.
Analysis_Required: Confidence explanation: decompose the recommendation into hard constraints, observations, lookups, calculations and forecasts; report coverage, freshness, missingness, model error, source conflict, sensitivity to preferences and the condition that should trigger a recheck or switch to the backup.
Answer_Boundary: A confidence label is not a probability of personal satisfaction unless it is calibrated for that outcome. Do not hide missing criteria inside a single score. Withdraw any component that lacks permitted provenance or valid coverage.

Question: A recurring temperature or ventilation problem was marked as fixed. Do comparable occupied periods show that conditions have returned to their normal range?
Notes: Gives students transparent evidence about whether a repeatedly reported problem has improved.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required telemetry: the same correctly located room and serving-system variables that established the fault, plus equipment command/feedback and relevant energy where appropriate; stable pre/post sensor placement, calibration, clock alignment, health and coverage are essential. Require current meter topology, aligned intervals and explicit treatment of shared loads and gaps.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: exact work-order scope and completion time, asset/room relationships, operating state, timetable/occupancy, weather, setpoints, overrides and later recurrence reports. Current topology must be verified operationally.
Analysis_Required: Repair verification: compare time-matched occupied periods before and after the recorded intervention, adjusting for occupancy, weather, schedule and operating state; test persistence, not one favourable reading; report effect size, uncertainty and remaining anomalies.
Answer_Boundary: The work-order status alone does not prove restoration, and improved room conditions do not prove which repair caused them. If pre/post periods or sensor configuration are not comparable, report the evidence as inconclusive and keep the official maintenance route.

Question: What sensors, building systems and official data sources support this answer, where are they located, and how recent and reliable are they?
Notes: Allows students to inspect the basis of an analytical answer rather than trusting fluent text alone.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: Required evidence is provenance rather than a new measurement: sensor or system identifier, observed property, unit, exact room/served zone, mounting or endpoint, sampling/aggregation, latest timestamp, calibration/commissioning, health, missingness and transformation history for every source used. Use aggregate service or endpoint health only; do not inspect content, credentials or identifiable traffic.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources: sensor and asset registry, ontology/knowledge-graph relationships, BMS or service inventory, data catalogue, calibration and maintenance records, access-control policy and the version of any threshold, model or external document applied.
Analysis_Required: Provenance lookup: list every permitted sensor/system source, observed property, room or served zone, timestamp, sampling/aggregation window, calibration or commissioning state, current health, missingness and transformation used in the answer; identify indirect or omitted evidence.
Answer_Boundary: Do not reveal credentials, connection strings, exact security-system topology, personal data or unauthorised maintenance detail. If a claim has no permitted traceable source, remove or qualify it; provenance completeness is part of answerability.

Question: Can you tell me whether this room is safe or compliant to use, or do I need to specify the particular hazard or requirement?
Notes: Prevents a high-consequence student question from receiving a generic answer and directs it to the correct evidence and authority.
Section: 8. Sustainability, faults, evidence and responsible use
Sensors_Required: No generic sensor package can answer this question. Evidence must be selected only after the student names the hazard or requirement: certified alarm or specialist detector status, calibrated environmental measurement, authoritative access/closure state or another competent-system source. Preserve source authority, location, timestamp, quality and coverage.
Authoritative_Sources: Authoritative current sources depend on the clarified issue: applicable Welsh or University requirement, current room use, risk assessment, certified safety system, inspection/maintenance record, official incident message, competent owner and student permission. The May 2021 plan is not compliance evidence.
Analysis_Required: Clarification + evidence-obligation assessment: ask whether the concern is fire, gas, electrical, air quality, access, occupancy, specialist activity or a named requirement; map the clarified claim to the correct authoritative systems, measurements, spatial/temporal coverage and competent owner; return observation/lookup, supported assessment, conflicting evidence or not assessable.
Answer_Boundary: Never answer broad safety or compliance from general environmental IoT data or an LLM judgement. Do not delay evacuation or override official instructions. For an immediate hazard, follow alarms, staff and emergency services; when authority or evidence is incomplete, return not assessable and provide the competent contact.

Question: Over the next four weeks, I need several four-hour thesis-writing blocks. When and where am I most likely to find a quiet, comfortable workspace that I am permitted to use?
Notes: Helps the doctoral researcher protect scarce deep-work time across an irregular month while understanding that future space availability is probabilistic.
Section: 1. Long-horizon planning, irregular schedules and focused work
Sensors_Required: Room-level temperature, RH, direct NDIR CO2, task-area illuminance and locally calculated LAeq/L10/L90; anonymous room occupancy and corridor footfall. Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: privacy-minimised briefing publication, acknowledgement and shift-coverage telemetry. Coverage: only the roles, locations, times and practical actions needed for the event/service; no personal health or casework systems. Timing/alignment: on approved briefing issue/update and at shift handover; use a common clock. Aggregation: by role/shift and task, not by attendee or diagnosis. Quality gate: require approved minimum-information briefing, current role roster, permission, version control and human scenario/knowledge check for critical actions. Privacy guard: No diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, casework, personal emergency-plan records detail or personal narrative; identify a person only when operationally necessary and authorised. Known limits: acknowledgement does not prove understanding, competence, recall or correct action in context; missing, stale or unhealthy evidence is unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and primary records: the approved event/service plan, role roster, practical task instructions and escalation contacts (the event/service owner, Security, accessibility/inclusion team and relevant operational owners). Corroborating sources: the person's consented minimum practical instruction where an individual arrangement is necessary. Precedence: the event/service owner approves the role briefing; the person controls individual disclosure; current incident command overrides routine briefing. Evidence record: retain source owner and version, access permission, provenance, and effective, observed and retrieved times for every claim. Stale when: an acknowledgement to a superseded version, roster after shift change or instruction outside its effective period. Conflict handling: keep disagreement visible and refer it to the event/service duty owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation: minimum-information briefing coverage and competency check. Decision interval: briefing issue through the operational shift. Minimum evidence: current approved briefing, every critical role covered, acknowledgement and a checked escalation path. Method: map critical tasks to roles/shifts, test a small set of scenario questions and expose uncovered periods without adding personal explanations. Quantified uncertainty: report critical-evidence completeness as n/N, plus critical roles briefed/required, scenario checks passed and uncovered minutes; 100% critical-role coverage is required for ready status. Safe failure: brief the missing role, add an authorised supervisor or remove/alter the dependent activity until coverage is verified.
Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. Do not disclose diagnosis, health, casework or personal emergency-plan records information, infer a person's needs, promise staff behaviour or replace professional training and supervision. Briefings must contain task-level instructions only and must not expose a diagnosis, case history or reason for the chosen requirement. Do not certify accessibility or safety, promise an outcome, grant access, authorise an exception or control an asset. Decision authority remains with the person, event/service owner, Security and operational line managers.

Question: Are general emergency and disruption instructions available in accessible formats with the current competent owner and contact route clearly shown?

Aggregation: by message/version, zone and channel, never by individual. Privacy guard: No health, casework or personal emergency-plan records, person tracking or inference about who needs assistance. Authoritative_Sources: Owners and primary records: current general emergency plan, incident procedures, public instructions, competent owner contacts and authorised message templates (Emergency Planning, Fire Safety, Security and building/service owners). Corroborating sources: current incident command instructions and competent exercises/tests. Precedence: incident command and competent emergency owners always outrank generated guidance, telemetry, routine plans, room bookings and historical maps. Evidence record: retain source owner and version, access permission, provenance, and effective, observed and retrieved times for every claim. Stale when: any plan/contact after a superseding approval, channel status beyond its incident age limit or test before a material system/process change. Conflict handling: keep disagreement visible and refer it to incident command or the competent emergency plan owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation: general-arrangement publication and cross-format readiness check. Decision interval: normal operation, planned event and any active incident period. Minimum evidence: current owner-approved general instructions, current contact route and equivalent essential content in every promised format/channel. Method: compare action/location/time/contact elements, verify channel delivery and label all person-specific decisions as requiring direct competent planning. Quantified uncertainty: report critical-evidence completeness as n/N, plus essential elements matched/total, channels/zones tested and plan/contact version age; any critical mismatch blocks a complete publication claim. Safe failure: publish only current owner-approved facts and contacts, identify the unavailable format/channel and defer all incident action to command.
Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. General information must not be presented as a personal emergency plan or as confirmation that assistance will be available. Question: Can the service desk arrange route assistance, portable seating or equipment through one authorised hand-off without making the person repeat sensitive information?

Quantified uncertainty: report critical-evidence completeness as n/N, plus critical tasks verified/total, overdue dependencies and oldest evidence age; all critical tasks must be verified before stating ready. Safe failure: escalate the exact task, communicate the practical limitation once, and offer a verified alternative without seeking additional sensitive detail.

Question: Will a room move, cancellation or delay reach attendees and accompanying people through selected channels before they decide to travel?
Notes: Enables the team to act before travel, avoid inconsistent versions and focus manual contact on the cases that still lack an authorised delivery route.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: authorised contact-channel, message-version and delivery-status telemetry. Coverage: the affected event/session contacts and public channels only; accompanying-person contacts included only with explicit permission. Timing/alignment: on approved change publication, delivery attempt and retry until the decision deadline; use a common clock. Aggregation: by message version, channel and event; minimise person-level retention. Quality gate: require current authorised contact set, selected channels, approved message, clock alignment within 1 minute, privacy permission and traceable minimal retention. Privacy guard: no identity, tracking, raw audio/images or person-level history. Known limits: delivery does not prove attention, comprehension, current contact details or successful rerouting; missing, stale or unhealthy evidence is unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and primary records: the approved booking/event change, authoritative room/route status, contact list and communication preferences valid for the event (the event/session owner, Timetabling/Space Management and institutional contact/channel owners). Precedence: the event/operational owner confirms the change; the event owner controls recipients and message; current version outranks earlier delivery attempts. Evidence record: retain source owner and version, access permission, provenance, and effective, observed and retrieved times for every claim. Stale when: contact/preferences outside the event purpose, message superseded, or delivery after the last useful decision time. Conflict handling: keep disagreement visible and refer it to the event/session owner and contact-data owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation: deadline-aware authorised notification coverage. Decision interval: change approval to the last useful travel/reroute decision time. Minimum evidence: one current approved message, authorised recipient/channel set and at least one viable delivery route for each contact where person-level status is permitted. Method: deduplicate, send the current version, compare delivery timestamps with the decision deadline and separate attendee/companion permissions. Quantified uncertainty: report critical-evidence completeness as n/N, plus successful authorised channel/contacts, version conflicts and late/unknown cases; never equate delivery with understanding or attendance. Safe failure: escalate unknown cases to the event owner for an authorised alternative and prepare verified on-site route/help arrangements.

Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. Do not disclose why a person needs a channel or companion contact, infer attendance, contact anyone without authority, promise receipt or reuse preferences across events. Do not certify accessibility or safety, promise an outcome, grant access, authorise an exception or control an asset. Decision authority remains with the person, event/session owner and contact/channel owners.

Question: Which aggregate demand patterns justify changes to staffing, equipment, service hours or event support without profiling any individual?
Notes: Supports transparent staffing and equipment planning while exposing hidden demand, coverage gaps and the uncertainty around any scenario.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: privacy-safe task counts, equipment bookings, service contacts, queue bands and anonymous attendance/zone counts. Coverage: defined services, assets, events and time bands with no person linkage across visits or datasets. Timing/alignment: operational events at source; analysis in weekly, termly or annual planning windows; use a common clock. Aggregation: by service type, location and time band with small-cell suppression. Quality gate: require consistent definitions, current permissions, provenance, deduplication rules, >=80% period coverage and suppression of cells below 10. Privacy guard: No diagnosis, health or casework/personal emergency-plan records data, person-level histories, demographic inference or cross-service linkage. Known limits: recorded demand excludes unmet or unreported need, service design affects contact volume and counts do not reveal why support was requested; missing, stale or unhealthy evidence is unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and primary records: current service definitions, staffing rotas, equipment inventory, event/timetable plans and approved operational demand records (the accessibility/inclusion team, service owners, Events/Timetabling, HR/workforce owners and equipment owners). Corroborating sources: structured barrier feedback and known periods of service interruption or changed eligibility. Precedence: owners define service scope and denominators; current operational changes must be reflected before comparing periods; aggregate analytics do not set staffing automatically. Evidence record: retain source owner and version, access permission, provenance, and effective, observed and retrieved times for every claim. Stale when: data before a definition/service/process change without harmonisation or periods with <80% coverage. Conflict handling: keep disagreement visible and refer it to the relevant service owner with institutional workforce/resource governance.
Analysis_Required: Operation: privacy-preserving demand, capacity and scenario analysis. Decision interval: agreed weekly/termly planning periods and named future event scenarios. Minimum evidence: consistent demand definitions, usable denominator/context, current staffing/equipment capacity and at least 8 comparable periods for trend/forecast claims. Method: calculate rates and peak distributions, distinguish contacts from completed support and test reversible staffing/equipment scenarios without predicting individuals. Quantified uncertainty: report critical-evidence completeness as n/N, plus counts, suppressed cells, 95% intervals, missingness and scenario ranges; no forecast when definitions changed or comparable periods <8. Safe failure: use qualitative owner judgement, commission better aggregate capture and trial a limited reversible resource change.
Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. Do not infer disability prevalence, diagnosis, individual future demand, distress or productivity; identify small groups; or automate staffing, eligibility or funding decisions. Do not turn aggregate service demand into a prediction about any named person, group identity or future attendance. Do not certify accessibility or safety, promise an outcome, grant access, authorise an exception or control an asset. Decision authority remains with service owners, workforce/resource governance and affected communities.

Question: Which new barriers were reported or detected today, what essential function do they affect, and which competent owner must respond first?
Notes: Provides the team with one actionable live queue with the right owner and interim communication instead of fragmented sensor alarms and reports.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: asset fault/heartbeat, route/room/service state and privacy-minimised structured barrier-report telemetry. Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, health or severity from reporter identity, expose reporter details, close/control an asset, or replace emergency/safety triage. Question: Which barriers recur after earlier tickets were closed at the same asset, place or service, and when should a root-cause investigation be triggered?
Notes: Enables the team to escalate chronic failures, challenge premature closure and invest in root-cause work rather than repeatedly treating symptoms.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: versioned barrier tickets, asset fault/state, maintenance completion and privacy-safe structured feedback telemetry. Coverage: the same mapped asset/location/service across incidents, remedial works and verified post-work observations. Timing/alignment: on each report, fault, completion and verification event; analyse in agreed monthly/termly windows; use a common clock. Aggregation: by asset/location and failure mode, never by reporter or affected person. Quality gate: require stable asset/location IDs, current owner mapping, provenance, permissions, comparable definitions and acceptable closure evidence for each resolved episode. Privacy guard: No reporter identity in trend outputs, no health or casework data and no linkage to personal schedules or attendance. Known limits: duplicate reporting, changed definitions, incomplete closure evidence and differing exposure can create false recurrence patterns; missing, stale or unhealthy evidence is unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and primary records: current work orders, closure reasons, remedial work evidence, post-work verification and asset/service change history (the relevant service owner, Estates/Facilities/IT/AV as applicable and the accessibility/inclusion team). Corroborating sources: competent inspection findings and structured barrier reports. Precedence: competent root-cause findings and current asset condition outrank ticket labels; a closed ticket without acceptable verification is not a resolved barrier. Evidence record: retain source owner and version, access permission, provenance, and effective, observed and retrieved times for every claim. Stale when: episodes before an asset redesign/definition change unless explicitly harmonised, or closure evidence outside the approved verification method. Conflict handling: keep disagreement visible and refer it to the competent asset/service owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation: recurrence detection and root-cause assessment trigger. Decision interval: a defined rolling 6- or 12-month improvement window. Minimum evidence: at least two independently verified post-closure recurrences of the same functional failure, with comparable exposure/context and current ownership. Method: link episodes by stable asset and failure mode, measure time-to-recurrence, distinguish unresolved from genuinely restored, and assess maintenance and change context. Quantified uncertainty: report critical-evidence completeness as n/N, plus recurrence count, time-to-recurrence range and 95% interval for rate when a denominator exists; do not call recurrence from unverified duplicates. Safe failure: retain a suspected-recurrence flag, commission competent inspection/root-cause assessment and stop repeating the same unverified fix.
Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. Do not attribute recurrence to users or staff without investigation, identify reporters, infer personal impact, or auto-direct disciplinary or procurement action. Do not certify accessibility or safety, promise an outcome, grant access, authorise an exception or control an asset. Decision authority remains with the competent asset/service owner and governance body.

Authoritative_Sources: Owners and primary records: current barrier severity/triage procedure, service targets, owner assignments, closure authority and acceptable evidence definitions (the accessibility/inclusion team, Estates/Facilities/IT/AV/Security and relevant service governance owners). Corroborating sources: competent triage, interim arrangement evidence and post-resolution verification. Method: calculate acknowledgement, interim-control and resolution times separately; pause clocks only under explicit policy and independently check all overrides. Pause or reset service clocks only under an explicit rule, and expose every override in the case evidence. Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. Do not certify accessibility or safety, promise an outcome, grant access, authorise an exception or control an asset. Answer_Boundary: Use only requirements the person chooses to state for this purpose and interval. Do not infer disability, diagnosis, health, neurotype, distress, capability or support need; identify or track people; use health, casework or personal emergency-plan records; or disclose beyond authorised need-to-know. Continuous cameras are neither required nor appropriate. Coverage and timing. Event-driven at installation, change and inspection; retain original capture time and version; aggregate to mismatch type and location, not image analytics alone. Quality and limits. Verify capture-device clock/UTC offset, image hash, sign/label ID, checker identity and source-version provenance. Calibration is not applicable, but image resolution, glare and OCR confidence must be recorded. Flag duplicate IDs and stale templates; never infer text not legible in the source. OCR may misread text; a photograph does not show visibility under all lighting or viewing conditions, physical mounting, accessibility or user understanding.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and precedence. The fire-safety lead owns emergency information content; Estates/Space Management owns current locations and layouts; the asset/system owner owns identifiers; Communications may own approved public wording. Current approved plan/instruction and signed change decision first; then signage/asset registers and competent inspection; OCR or scan output is supporting evidence only. Times, access and provenance. Detailed emergency plans, secure asset locations and raw images are role-restricted; public output uses only approved wording. Retain effective, observed and retrieved times, source ID, version or signature, and the transformation used. Immediately stale after a route, asset, naming or emergency-plan change; otherwise by the inspection schedule. Conflict. Any text, version, location or identifier mismatch remains open for owner decision; analytics cannot choose which document is authoritative. Spatial claims require current owner-approved mapping; the May 2021 floor plan is historical reference only.
Analysis_Required: Operation and interval. Lookup, text comparison and spatial consistency check; recommendation is limited to inspect, replace or reconcile through the owner. After each approved change and in scheduled inspection summaries. Minimum evidence and method. A current approved source document, sign/label ID and location, legible captured evidence, assessment date and current change record. Compare exact controlled wording, symbol/version, destination and location against the approved source; flag uncertain OCR for human assessment rather than auto-correcting. Uncertainty and safe failure. Capture quality, OCR confidence, hidden signs, unrecorded relocation and current-plan uncertainty. Return 'sign/label agreement not demonstrated' and require attended verification.
Answer_Boundary: Do not publish or rewrite emergency instructions, infer compliance from OCR, or declare a route correct because signs agree with each other. Do not expose secure drawings, equipment locations or unapproved emergency wording. Do not disclose personal emergency evacuation plans, identities, individual movement or security-sensitive detail beyond authorised need. Do not certify fire safety, authorise work or impairments, operate or reset life-safety systems, issue emergency instructions, or override the Responsible Person, fire service or current emergency plan.
