Sensors_Required: No sensor can determine accountability or competence. A proposed duty-status feed may show team-level coverage, not a person's whereabouts. Timing: use only approved rota windows; disclose no badge history. Evidence quality: report feed age, update cadence, permission scope and any unavailable or unmatched roles. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the risk-register owner and accountable local manager; supporting sources: the approved role directory, delegation register and duty rota owner. Precedence: the named approved risk owner and recorded delegation outrank directory guesses, email signatures or access events. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: one business day for duty coverage and the register review date for ownership. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup and comparison. Decision interval: daily and before time-critical work or events. Minimum evidence: a live risk ID, current owner field and valid delegation window. Method: ownership join, delegation validation and gap detection; join risk, role and rota records without inferring presence; distinguish vacant, absent, unverified and permission-denied states. Uncertainty: A stale rota, a delegation not yet effective, a vacant role or an unmatched risk identifier can falsely imply cover. Safe failure: Return Owner or deputy not confirmed and escalate to the accountable manager before a time-critical decision.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer availability, competence or accountability from badge use, calendar gaps or telemetry, and do not reassign a duty.

Question: Which risk assessments require competent review now because a material change, incident, complaint, inspection finding or verified control failure has occurred?
Notes: Build a defensible reassessment queue, assign competent reviewers and act first on expired or materially changed high-consequence work.
Sensors_Required: Proposed triggers may include verified asset faults, service outages, changed room configuration, booking-type changes and incident timestamps. Timing: aggregate by assessment and day unless urgency requires events. Evidence quality: publish mapping, source health, clock alignment, false-trigger risk and missing integrations; a trigger is not proof of invalidity. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the risk-assessment register owner and activity owner; supporting sources: change control, incident management, Estates work orders and asset owners. Precedence: the approved assessment and formal review-trigger records outrank telemetry-derived cues. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: the stated review date, or immediately when a verified owner records a material trigger. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup and recommendation. Decision interval: daily, and within 15 minutes for verified safety-critical control loss. Minimum evidence: a current assessment linked to a due date or one verified trigger. Method: trigger-based review-queue generation; apply owner-approved trigger rules, deduplicate linked events and rank by consequence and evidence strength. Uncertainty: A trigger may be mislinked, duplicated, later withdrawn or timestamped differently from the assessment it appears to affect. Safe failure: Place the item in a human review queue as Trigger not confirmed; do not invalidate the assessment automatically.
Answer_Boundary: Do not declare an assessment invalid, determine legal sufficiency, invent a trigger from weak correlation or set a new review date for the owner.

Question: Which risk-register entries no longer match the current room use, equipment, occupancy assumptions, access arrangements or building services on which their controls depend?
Notes: Identify assessments that need correction or reassessment before their controls are relied upon, and send each mismatch to the risk, room or asset owner.
Sensors_Required: Proposed anonymous doorway counts, door and room-power states, and verified safety-service status may test only the operational assumptions named in a risk entry. Cover the exact mapped room, equipment and control dependency during the assessment window; use five- or fifteen-minute aggregates unless a fault event is required. Evidence envelope: show modality and installation point, mapping version, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test date, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Do not use telemetry to classify room use. Unmapped or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the risk-register owner, room owner and space-management owner; supporting sources: timetabling, Security closure logs, Estates handback and event owners. Precedence: a current formal closure or competent owner instruction outranks bookings, historical plans and telemetry; approved room-use records outrank inferred use. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 15 minutes for closures, one day for bookings and the owner-defined register review date. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, observation and comparison. Decision interval: before reliance on the assessment and after a material room, equipment, access or service change. Minimum evidence: current assessment version, named assumptions, current room/asset owner records and one verified observation or status source for each tested dependency. Method: compare each assumption with current controlled records and bounded observations; label untested assumptions separately. Uncertainty: Mapping age, unobserved assumptions, blind spots, aggregation loss and conflicting room or asset records can hide a mismatch. Safe failure: Return Assumption not verified and request current owner confirmation or competent inspection.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer a specific activity or unauthorised behaviour from occupancy, override a closure, or treat the May 2021 plan as proof of current room function.

Question: Which recorded risk controls depend on a safety-critical asset or service that is unavailable, impaired, in test or not currently verified?
Notes: Restrict, relocate or re-plan affected activity, raise the correct technical fault and track restoration of the depended-on control.
Sensors_Required: Proposed status feeds may cover mapped alarms, ventilation, local exhaust, emergency lighting, access release, water and power. Timing: use change events and 5-minute health summaries. Evidence quality: require verified dependency mapping, commissioning, applicable calibration, clock alignment and heartbeat; distinguish fault, maintenance, disabled and unknown states, and show unmonitored dependencies. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the risk/control owner and relevant technical asset owner; supporting sources: BMS, fire-system records, CMMS, commissioning certificates and approved impairment logs. Precedence: the competent asset owner or official safety-system panel state outranks a generic dashboard or inferred fault. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 5 minutes for live impairments and the latest approved dependency map. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, calculation and recommendation. Decision interval: within 5 to 15 minutes of a verified impairment. Minimum evidence: one approved control dependency plus a current authoritative asset state. Method: control-to-asset dependency graph evaluation and fault correlation; trace direct and upstream dependencies, avoid double counting and show alternative controls only when formally recorded. Uncertainty: Dependency maps may omit upstream services, a maintenance state may be ambiguous and a secondary dashboard may lag the official panel. Safe failure: Return Control availability unknown; do not rely on it until the asset owner confirms status and the risk owner decides any interim control.
Answer_Boundary: Do not automatically declare work safe or unsafe, reset or bypass equipment, invent substitute controls, or authorise continuation during an impairment.

Question: Where is ownership of safety decisions unresolved at interfaces between the university, building owner, service teams, event organisers and contractors?
Notes: Resolve interface ownership before work begins, document escalation routes and stop hazards falling between teams, landlords, contractors or services.
Sensors_Required: No sensor can assign responsibility. Proposed zone-use counts and service-status events may show that an interface is active, but only as aggregated context. Evidence quality: report location mapping, time window, permissions and missing coverage; never use individual movement or device ownership as evidence of duty. Timing: use event windows for active interfaces and a daily responsibility-gap summary. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the local accountable manager and health and safety governance owner; supporting sources: leases, service agreements, room ownership, event bookings, contractor scopes and project responsibility matrices. Precedence: formally approved responsibility allocations and current contractual arrangements outrank custom, assumptions and historical ownership. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: the latest signed issue or any recorded organisational change. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup and comparison. Decision interval: at each change, event mobilisation and monthly governance review. Minimum evidence: a defined activity/service interface plus current responsibility records. Method: responsibility-interface and RACI gap analysis; map each decision, control, handoff and escalation to an owner; identify overlaps, gaps and permission-limited evidence. Uncertainty: Contracts, local arrangements and responsibility matrices may overlap, use different terms or lag organisational change. Safe failure: Return Interface owner unresolved and escalate to the local accountable manager before interface-dependent work proceeds.
Answer_Boundary: Do not assign legal duties, reinterpret contracts, disclose commercially restricted terms or infer responsibility from who happens to be present.

Question: What safety evidence is still missing before the proposed change can be presented to the responsible owner for a start, approval or commissioning decision?
Notes: Give the responsible owner a precise hold list, assign missing tests or consultation, and prevent an unsupported change from reaching operation.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence may include asset-discovery changes, commissioning-test status, environmental baselines, door/route configuration and anonymous occupancy trials. Timing: use milestone snapshots, not continuous personal monitoring. Evidence quality: show mapping, test period, calibration, clock status, uptime and any untested modes. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the change owner, project manager and relevant safety/technical approvers; supporting sources: design records, commissioning results, risk assessments, room ownership and operational handback. Precedence: the approved change-control workflow and signed stage records outrank verbal agreement, telemetry or a planned completion date. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: the current project stage and latest approved version. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, comparison and recommendation. Decision interval: at each formal change-control gate and immediately before start, approval or commissioning. Minimum evidence: approved change scope, current hazard and risk record, consultation outcome, test plan, acceptance criteria, responsible owner and evidence for every safety dependency. Method: trace each gate criterion to a current record or verified test result; separate missing, failed, conditional and not-applicable items. Uncertainty: Untested interfaces, incomplete consultation, stale commissioning evidence and unresolved acceptance criteria can make a gate appear complete. Safe failure: Recommend Hold for evidence and give the responsible owner the exact missing tests, records or consultation; never approve the change.
Answer_Boundary: Do not approve the change, certify design or commissioning, accept residual risk, or treat a successful sensor reading as formal handback.

Question: Which risk-reduction actions are overdue, blocked, ownerless, duplicated or recorded complete without the verification required by the risk owner?
Notes: Recover stalled risk reduction, merge genuine duplicates and stop unsupported completion claims from hiding an active control gap.
Sensors_Required: Proposed work-order, asset-state and inspection-result telemetry may corroborate implementation. Timing: use daily status snapshots and event timestamps. Evidence quality: show asset mapping, completion evidence type, observation period, data latency and gaps; a closed work order or normal reading does not by itself prove control effectiveness. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the risk owner and corrective-action register owner; supporting sources: CMMS, project plans, procurement, budget owners and inspection records. Precedence: the risk owner's current action and residual-risk record outrank inferred priority; formal dependency and completion evidence outrank free-text status. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: one business day for action status and the next formal risk review for residual risk. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, comparison and recommendation. Decision interval: weekly, at governance review and before any action is closed. Minimum evidence: current action ID, risk link, owner, due date, dependency, completion claim and owner-defined verification requirement. Method: classify overdue, blocked, ownerless, duplicate and unverified-complete actions; keep risk priority separate from action age. Uncertainty: Action ages can be distorted by revised due dates, duplicate records, unlinked dependencies and unsupported completion claims. Safe failure: Keep the action open or Unknown and route closure, duplication and priority decisions to the risk owner.
Answer_Boundary: Do not close actions, calculate legal tolerability, lower a risk rating automatically, assign blame or reprioritise commitments without the owner.

Question: Do current operational plans include the authorised accessibility and individual-adjustment dependencies needed for the activity, without exposing personal or medical information?
Notes: Verify the enabling arrangement without exposing personal details, repair missing assets and consult through the authorised adjustment process.
Sensors_Required: No sensor may infer pregnancy, disability, health or assistance need. Proposed accessibility telemetry can cover only asset and route availability, such as lift status, powered-door status and refuge communication health, aggregated by zone. Evidence quality: show permission, mapping, uptime and gaps; no person-level linkage. Timing: use current asset state and authorised on-request checks aggregated by zone, with no person-level linkage. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the authorised adjustment-plan owner, occupational-health or HR service and emergency-planning owner; supporting sources: the individual, local manager, accessibility assessment and Estates asset owners. Precedence: the person-approved, need-to-know adjustment status and current emergency arrangement outrank generic assumptions; medical detail remains restricted. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: the agreed review date or any person-approved change. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup and comparison. Decision interval: on authorised request and after relevant space or service change. Minimum evidence: a permissioned control requirement, current location and asset status without diagnosis data. Method: privacy-preserving control-completeness and asset-dependency check; match required arrangements to available routes, services and contacts; suppress small-group outputs and expose missing consent or access. Uncertainty: The authorised plan may be access-restricted, time-limited or dependent on an asset whose location or service state is not current. Safe failure: Return Arrangement not verified and route the gap privately to the authorised adjustment-plan owner without disclosing the reason.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer a condition, create a medical or individual risk record, reveal the reason for an adjustment, or judge whether the person can undertake an activity.

Question: Which unresolved risks, weakly evidenced controls and time-critical owner decisions require formal escalation at the next safety governance meeting?
Notes: Run a focused governance meeting, separate decisions from information gaps and leave each action with an owner, deadline and evidence requirement.
Sensors_Required: Proposed dashboards may supply aggregated incidents, actions, asset impairments, inspection coverage, environmental exceptions and data-quality indicators. Timing: use weekly or monthly aggregates with suppressions for small groups. Evidence quality: state coverage, denominator, sampling, calibration, clock alignment, uptime and known blind spots. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the committee secretariat, health and safety governance owner and each contributing source owner; supporting sources: risk, incident, action, training, Estates and emergency-planning systems. Precedence: approved meeting scope and controlled source records outrank dashboard summaries; each source owner retains authority for interpretation. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: the reporting cut-off, with late changes clearly timestamped. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, calculation and recommendation. Decision interval: before each meeting and at the reporting cut-off. Minimum evidence: an approved agenda, reporting period, metric definitions and source-owner access. Method: evidence-pack assembly, completeness checking and provenance validation; compile only in-scope evidence, reconcile duplicates, label facts versus estimates and produce an exception list. Uncertainty: Reporting cut-offs, inconsistent risk scales, missing owners and selective source access can distort what appears most urgent. Safe failure: Issue an evidence-gap agenda rather than a recommendation and defer any unsupported decision to the accountable governance owner.
Answer_Boundary: Do not imply committee endorsement, hide adverse data, fill missing evidence with assumptions, or present an analytical summary as certification or legal assurance.

Question: Which escape routes, final exits, fire doors or refuge approaches need immediate physical inspection because status is obstructed, secured incorrectly, impaired or unknown?
Notes: Prioritise a physical route inspection, place an interim control through existing procedures and direct the fault to the correct owner.
Sensors_Required: Proposed door contacts, lock/release states and fixed time-of-flight or beam sensors at agreed choke points can flag change, not prove route clearance. Timing: use events plus 5-minute summaries during occupancy. Evidence quality: publish exact coverage, obstruction-detection limits, commissioning, clock alignment, battery/uptime and false-alarm history. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the fire-safety responsible person and current emergency-plan owner; supporting sources: the door register, Security closure log, Estates faults and competent inspection records. Precedence: a formal closure or competent fire-safety instruction outranks sensor state; current fire strategy and door designation outrank the historical floor plan. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 5 minutes for operational status and the latest approved fire-safety record. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: observation and recommendation. Decision interval: live to 5 minutes while the building is occupied. Minimum evidence: a mapped designated route or door plus one current authoritative state and usable telemetry where installed. Method: rule-based exception detection and source reconciliation; detect held-open, locked, unavailable and possible obstruction states; require human confirmation for ambiguous physical conditions. Uncertainty: Contacts and beams cannot see every obstruction, door-leaf defect or refuge condition; mapping, test mode and status latency may also mislead. Safe failure: Return Route not physically verified and request immediate competent inspection while retaining any existing restriction.
Answer_Boundary: A door contact, beam or counter must not be presented as proof that an escape route is physically clear. Do not certify an escape route, infer why a door is open, identify occupants, unlock or lock a door, order evacuation, or replace competent fire inspection.

Question: Which reported locations need prompt inspection for slip, trip, collision, falling-object or route-obstruction hazards, and what immediate control is already recorded?
Notes: Send an inspector to the right location, confirm the temporary control already in place, and escalate cleaning, cordoning, repair or storage action through the responsible owner.
Sensors_Required: Proposed leak ropes, local floor-moisture sensors, door/route obstruction sensors and lighting status may cover known high-risk points. Timing: use event alerts and 5-minute persistence. Evidence quality: show installation footprint, surface sensitivity, cleaning interference, calibration, clock status, uptime and blind spots; most floor hazards still require inspection. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the local area manager and inspection/cleaning service owners; supporting sources: incident and near-miss reports, Estates faults, Security reports and active work zones. Precedence: a verified report or competent inspection outranks a sensor cue; formal closures and work-zone controls outrank normal route status. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 5 minutes for active hazards and one shift for routine reports. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: observation and recommendation. Decision interval: within 5 to 15 minutes for alerts and each inspection round. Minimum evidence: one verified high-confidence alert or two independent lower-confidence cues in the same zone. Method: conservative hazard-cue ranking; combine persistence, route criticality, occupancy opportunity and recent reports; suppress ranking where coverage is absent. Uncertainty: The reported location may be imprecise, the condition transient, the sensor cue false and the recorded temporary control stale. Safe failure: Return Hazard not confirmed, dispatch a site check and treat the immediate-control state as Unknown until observed.
Answer_Boundary: Do not treat a report or sensor cue as proof of a hazard, decide that a route is safe without inspection, or disclose a reporter unnecessarily. No safety or compliance certification, work authorisation or asset control.

Question: Which routes or task areas need a competent lighting assessment because failed luminaires or screening measurements may not support safe movement or work?
Notes: Target luminaire repair, temporary lighting, relocation or a formal illuminance survey at the affected route or task plane.
Sensors_Required: Proposed calibrated lux sensors at representative route and task-plane locations, plus luminaire-driver or circuit status, may support screening. Timing: use 1-minute readings and 15-minute summaries for the mapped route or task area. Evidence quality: show sensor height and orientation, daylight influence, calibration date, clock alignment, coverage, uptime and outliers; one fixed sensor is not room-wide evidence. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the Estates lighting asset owner and local area/activity owner; supporting sources: lighting design information, inspection records, fault tickets and current room use. Precedence: competent design or inspection criteria for the actual task outrank generic thresholds and telemetry; verified circuit faults outrank inferred failure. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 15 minutes for readings and the latest approved task/use information. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: observation and comparison. Decision interval: every 15 minutes during relevant use and on fault events. Minimum evidence: a commissioned representative sensor or verified luminaire fault plus current task/route context. Method: threshold and persistence screening against locally approved criteria; compare time-matched values, account for daylight and sensor uncertainty, and identify areas requiring a competent lighting survey. Uncertainty: Sensor position may not represent the task plane, daylight and screening can change rapidly, and calibration or luminaire mapping may be wrong. Safe failure: Return Lighting adequacy unknown and arrange a competent survey or temporary owner-approved control without a compliance claim.
Answer_Boundary: A fixed lux reading must not be treated as a task-specific lighting assessment across an unmeasured area. Do not certify lighting compliance, infer personal visual ability, treat a sensor outside the task plane as exposure evidence, or switch circuits.

Question: Which occupied work zones need competent investigation because temperature, humidity, carbon-dioxide or ventilation-service evidence is outside the approved screening envelope?
Notes: Select zones for competent workplace-condition investigation, check ventilation or controls and avoid broad claims from isolated measurements.
Sensors_Required: Proposed temperature, relative-humidity and CO2 sensors, plus supply-airflow or plant state where available, may support a workplace-condition screen. Timing: sample each minute and report 15-minute and hourly summaries for mapped occupied zones. Evidence quality: show placement, calibration, drift, clock alignment, coverage, uptime and sensor saturation; CO2 is a ventilation proxy, not exposure or health evidence. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the Estates HVAC owner and local activity/room owner; supporting sources: BMS, room-use records, approved workplace-condition criteria, complaints and maintenance faults. Precedence: a competent investigation and current operating instruction outrank dashboard thresholds; verified plant faults outrank inferred ventilation quality. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 15 minutes for conditions, 5 minutes for plant faults and the current activity window. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: observation and comparison. Decision interval: every 15 minutes while occupied, with immediate review for verified plant loss. Minimum evidence: usable environmental data for the occupied interval plus current room use and sensor-health evidence. Method: persistence, anomaly and occupancy-context screening; compare against owner-approved screening bands, detect sustained deviation and distinguish local sensor anomaly from zone-wide evidence. Uncertainty: Placement, occupancy context, outdoor conditions, HVAC response lag and the limited interpretation of carbon-dioxide readings affect the screen. Safe failure: Return Screening exception or coverage insufficient and request competent workplace-condition investigation without diagnosing exposure or harm.
Answer_Boundary: CO2 and environmental readings are screening evidence only and must not be used to diagnose symptoms, exposure or ventilation compliance. Do not diagnose heat stress, illness or poor health, certify ventilation or indoor-air safety, infer who was exposed, or command HVAC operation.

Question: Which areas need a competent occupational-noise survey because plant, alarms or temporary work may be producing elevated area sound?
Notes: Commission a competent noise survey at the right location and time, then plan engineering or administrative controls from valid measurements.
Sensors_Required: Proposed integrating sound-level meters can record privacy-preserving LAeq and peak summaries without storing audio or speech. Timing: use 1-minute values and 15-minute aggregates at defined locations. Evidence quality: show microphone class, placement, calibration before/after, clock alignment, wind/impact artefacts, coverage and uptime; fixed area sound is not personal dose. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the activity or equipment owner and occupational safety/noise adviser; supporting sources: work permits, equipment schedules, previous acoustic surveys, complaints and maintenance records. Precedence: a competent noise assessment and approved task controls outrank fixed-sensor screening; task timing records outrank inferred source attribution. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 15 minutes for screening and the current permit/activity window. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: observation, estimate and recommendation. Decision interval: every 15 minutes during relevant work and after complaints. Minimum evidence: a calibrated meter with usable data plus verified task or equipment timing. Method: area-noise event detection and source-time correlation; compare to locally approved screening triggers, separate background and transient events, and request personal or task-specific assessment where needed. Uncertainty: Meter position, reflections, short peaks, source attribution and calibration determine whether an area summary represents the task. Safe failure: Return Noise risk not established and commission a competent occupational-noise survey before selecting controls.
Answer_Boundary: Area sound summaries must not be converted into an individual noise dose, hearing-risk judgement or medical conclusion. Do not record speech, infer hearing damage or personal exposure, identify a speaker or worker, certify compliance, or shut down equipment.

Question: Which storage, stacking, housekeeping, waste or aisle-clearance conditions require a site check, and which evidence is only a report rather than a verified observation?

Evidence quality: show exact instrumented footprint, load-cell capacity/calibration, object-detection limitations, clock alignment, uptime and unmonitored shelves; visual inspection remains primary. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the store or area owner and local inspection owner; supporting sources: inventory records, fire/route plans, cleaning reports, work orders and competent rack inspections. Notes: Withdraw or caveat unreliable claims, repair mapping or source health and re-commission the evidence route before reuse.
Sensors_Required: Proposed source-health telemetry should expose sensor and gateway heartbeat, mapped asset or zone, calibration due date, clock offset, latency, retained gaps, aggregation configuration and permission failures. Timing: evaluate live health every 5 minutes and publish a daily quality summary by evidence route. Evidence quality: a healthy device does not prove correct placement, representativeness or semantic mapping; independent inspection and owner confirmation remain necessary. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the telemetry platform owner and each physical sensor/asset owner; supporting sources: commissioning certificates, calibration records, mapping register, change tickets and data-quality rules. Precedence: current commissioning and calibration status outrank observed data volume; source-owner fault declarations outrank automated health scores. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 5 minutes for live health and the current commissioning/calibration record. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: observation, calculation and comparison. Decision interval: with every answer, daily dashboard review and after system change. Minimum evidence: the claim's required sensors plus current health, mapping, time and calibration evidence. Method: data-quality rule evaluation and claim-level reliability tracing; propagate source quality into the answer, identify unsupported zones/intervals and return unknown when minimum quality fails. Uncertainty: A heartbeat cannot prove correct location, mapping, calibration or representativeness, and aggregation or permission gaps can hide failure. Safe failure: Withdraw or caveat the claim and recommission the evidence route before it supports another decision.
Answer_Boundary: A healthy device heartbeat must not be treated as proof of correct placement, calibration, mapping or representativeness. Do not infer absence of hazard from absence of data, hide downtime, extrapolate across unmapped rooms, certify sensor accuracy or alter calibration records.

Question: Across comparable locations and periods, is a strategic control programme associated with sustained improvement, and what alternative explanations remain?
Notes: Decide whether to continue evaluation, adapt implementation, target further investigation or commission a stronger comparison without overstating impact.
Sensors_Required: Proposed before/after indicators should be selected in advance and measured with stable sensors, placement, aggregation and privacy settings. Timing: use daily or weekly values over comparable periods. Evidence quality: show calibration, clock alignment, uptime, coverage changes, seasonality, activity volume and competing interventions; no personal outcome tracking. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the improvement owner and risk owner; supporting sources: change-control record, baseline assessment, incident/inspection data, commissioning and affected activity owners. Precedence: the predefined evaluation plan and competent review outrank post-hoc favourable metrics; adverse findings and changed operations remain visible. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: after the agreed minimum observation period and at scheduled review. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: calculation, comparison and estimate. Decision interval: at the pre-agreed programme review points. Minimum evidence: a documented theory of change, stable indicator definition, comparable baseline and follow-up periods, exposure denominator, implementation dates, source-quality record and relevant concurrent changes. Method: use a pre-specified interrupted time series, matched comparison or stratified before/after analysis; test sensitivity to season, reporting and activity volume. Uncertainty: Confidence intervals, power, residual confounding, implementation variation, concurrent changes and alternative explanations limit attribution. Safe failure: Report Association not established and continue or redesign the evaluation rather than claiming that the programme caused improvement.
Answer_Boundary: Do not infer causation from a simple before/after change, hide adverse patterns through aggregation, or declare the programme effective without comparable evidence. No safety or compliance certification or continuation authorisation.

Question: Which proposed actions should enter the next improvement plan when consequence, exposure opportunity, commitments, feasibility, dependencies and evidence strength are considered together?
Notes: Build a defensible improvement plan, sequence dependencies, assign owners and direct resources to actions with the strongest risk-reduction case.
Sensors_Required: Proposed telemetry may quantify control availability, exposure opportunities, repeat faults and evidence gaps at aggregated zone/asset level. Timing: use monthly or quarterly summaries. Evidence quality: show denominator, coverage, calibration, clock alignment, uptime and uncertainty; sensing should support, not replace consultation, engineering judgement or formal commitments. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the health and safety governance/risk owners and accountable budget owners; supporting sources: risk register, incident lessons, audit findings, consultation, asset plans, commitments and feasibility studies. Precedence: mandatory or formally committed actions and competent risk judgement outrank analytical ranking; approved strategy and budget decisions remain authoritative. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: annual/quarterly planning and after major incidents or changes. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: calculation and recommendation. Decision interval: quarterly and annual planning cycles. Minimum evidence: candidate actions, criteria definitions, owner ratings, cost/feasibility ranges and evidence quality. Method: transparent multi-criteria decision analysis with sensitivity testing; show weighted and unweighted rankings, dependencies, uncertainty and distributional effects; retain owner rationale and dissent. Uncertainty: Weights, cost and feasibility ranges, mandatory obligations, dependencies and distributional effects can make a ranking unstable. Safe failure: Show sensitivity and unresolved criteria, then route the choice to governance; do not accept risk or approve budget.
Answer_Boundary: A weighted ranking is advisory and must not accept risk, displace mandatory commitments or replace consultation and competent judgement. Do not determine legal obligation, approve budget, accept residual risk, hide consultation needs, or present a ranking as an authorisation.

Question: Where do authoritative systems conflict about owner, asset, zone, closure, permit, action or completion status, and who must resolve each conflict?
Notes: Send each conflict to the authoritative owner, prevent contradictory instructions and correct master data at source.
Sensors_Required: Proposed observed states may help expose a conflict but cannot settle governance. Timing: use event timestamps and daily reconciliation. Evidence quality: show mapping confidence, clock alignment, latency, uptime and sensor-interpretation limits; keep each source and its provenance separate rather than overwriting with a blended value. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the owners of every conflicting source and the health and safety service owner; supporting sources: risk, space, access, CMMS, permit, incident and project systems. Precedence: the published source-precedence rule applies by field; where equal or undefined, no automated winner is selected and owners must resolve. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: 5 minutes for live operational states and one day for administrative records. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: comparison and recommendation. Decision interval: with every query and daily reconciliation. Minimum evidence: two permissioned sources referring to the same asset/location/control and their effective/retrieval times. Method: field-level conflict detection, precedence application and unresolved-issue register; compare identifiers, versions, states and time validity, apply approved precedence and retain the losing value and reason. Uncertainty: Identifiers, effective times, replication lag, permissions and an undefined field-level precedence rule can prevent resolution. Safe failure: Return Source conflict unresolved, suppress the derived decision and route the exact field conflict to its authoritative owner.
Answer_Boundary: Do not silently choose a convenient source, overwrite records, infer owner intent, disclose restricted conflicts broadly or certify the resolved state.

Question: For each catalogue question and user role, are purpose, access, minimisation, retention, small-group protection and disclosure controls adequate?
Notes: Approve, redesign or deny the evidence route, tighten permissions and retention, and protect small groups before operational use.
Sensors_Required: Proposed governance telemetry may report role-based query counts, denied fields, small-group suppression, retention jobs and source-permission health without storing question content, identities or movement histories. Timing: use daily service totals and quarterly role-by-purpose review, suppressing small groups. Evidence quality: show configuration version, audit coverage, missing connectors, clock alignment and access-log retention; system logs cannot establish lawful purpose or fairness. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the information-governance/data-protection owner and each data source owner; supporting sources: approved purpose, privacy assessment, access-control policy, retention schedule and health and safety governance. Precedence: lawful or approved purpose, least-privilege decision and source-owner permission outrank analytical convenience; person consent or restricted records remain controlling. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: at design, permission change, new question and periodic review. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, comparison and recommendation. Decision interval: before access, on change and quarterly review. Minimum evidence: a defined question, user role, decision purpose, required fields, aggregation and retention need. Method: purpose-role-data policy mapping and least-privilege validation; test necessity, proportionality, minimisation, small-group risk, onward disclosure and deletion; deny or aggregate where controls fail. Uncertainty: Purpose can drift, combined data may become linkable, small groups may be re-identifiable and retention or role controls may fail. Safe failure: Deny, minimise or aggregate the evidence route until the information-governance and source owners approve the control set.
Answer_Boundary: Service logs must not be repurposed to inspect question content, reconstruct movement or create individual risk or medical records. Do not expand purpose, infer health or identity, combine datasets to track people, reveal restricted records, bypass permissions or retain data longer than authorised.

Question: Does the governance report clearly separate controlled lookup, direct observation, calculation, estimate, forecast, comparison, recommendation, unknown and stale evidence?
Notes: Let governance readers distinguish facts from estimates and recommendations, challenge weak claims and make decisions against visible uncertainty.
Sensors_Required: Proposed report metrics should carry source, numerator/denominator, aggregation, coverage, calibration, clock alignment, uptime, gaps and suppression status. Timing: use frozen reporting snapshots. Evidence quality: show changes in definitions and instrumentation; no metric should imply individual health, blame, productivity or complete building coverage. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the health and safety reporting owner and every metric source owner; supporting sources: approved metric dictionary, risk/incident/action systems, Estates and governance meeting scope. Precedence: controlled source records and metric definitions outrank visual summaries; owner corrections after cut-off are shown as dated amendments. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: the formal reporting cut-off and retrieval time. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, calculation and comparison. Decision interval: before each governance report is released. Minimum evidence: metric specification, numerator and denominator, source lineage, transformation code or rule, coverage, suppression, owner, period and evidence class. Method: tag every claim as controlled lookup, direct observation, calculation, estimate, forecast, comparison, recommendation, unknown or stale; verify that caveats follow the claim. Uncertainty: Missingness, measurement error, aggregation, denominator instability, changing definitions and unresolved source conflicts can alter a claim class. Safe failure: Withdraw or label the claim Unknown until its evidence class, transformation and lineage are reproducible.
Answer_Boundary: A polished report must not hide uncertainty or turn a recommendation into assurance, certification or authorisation. Do not claim compliance or assurance, hide adverse uncertainty, compare incompatible periods, infer personal outcomes or promise that reported trends will continue.

Question: Which health and safety decisions must remain outside the service because they require inspection, consultation, occupational-health, emergency, legal or other competent judgement?
Notes: Keep the service inside an approved decision-support role, route excluded decisions correctly and prioritise evidence improvements without creating unsafe automation.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence-coverage maps should list, for each question, available sensors and integrations, mapped assets or zones, timing, aggregation, calibration, clock status, uptime, permission and gaps. Timing: use live source health plus a quarterly capability snapshot. Evidence quality: explicitly mark uncommissioned, unmapped, stale, permission-denied and proxy-only routes; never substitute a weak proxy for missing evidence. Traceability: record modality/feed ID, exact installation point and mapped asset or zone, spatial and temporal coverage, sample and aggregation interval, calibration or functional-test state, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift or resets, permission and provenance. Unmapped, uncommissioned, stale, permission-denied or unhealthy evidence is unavailable.
Authoritative_Sources: Current owners and sources: the health and safety governance owner and each competent decision owner; supporting sources: legal, occupational-health, emergency, inspection, consultation and technical competence boundaries, service risk assessment and approved use cases. Precedence: applicable law, authorised emergency command, competent professional judgement and current organisational delegations outrank catalogue coverage or analytical capability. Metadata: record ID/version, owner, permission, effective time, observed or event time where relevant, retrieved time and lineage. Staleness: every governance, legal, professional or service-capability change; expose conflicts. Conflicts: retain competing states and route resolution to the relevant current owner and affected source owner. Retrieval recency, analytics and telemetry cannot override a controlled source.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup, comparison and recommendation. Decision interval: before enabling a question, quarterly and after any material system or governance change. Minimum evidence: a named decision, lawful purpose, accountable owner, evidence route and explicit boundary. Method: capability and prohibited-decision boundary mapping; classify answerable, partially answerable, inspection-only, professional-judgement, emergency-command and prohibited cases; test safe failure and permission. Uncertainty: Law, delegation, professional boundaries and source permissions can change, while technical capability can be mistaken for authority. Safe failure: Refuse the unsupported decision and route it to the named inspection, consultation, occupational-health, emergency, legal or competent process.
Answer_Boundary: Do not expand capability from technical availability, present the catalogue as legal advice, infer health, create medical or individual risk records, certify safety or compliance, accept risk, authorise work, command an emergency response or control safety-critical assets. Do not use the May 2021 floor plan as current operational truth.

Question: For the current declared exposure, which buildings, zones, fixed plant, portable equipment and contents are evidenced as included, and which items remain unmatched or ambiguous?
Notes: Enables the assessor to target a survey, request register correction, clarify the declared schedule and identify exposure concentrations before an accountable insurance decision.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Asset-tag or barcode inventories, approved BMS point lists, fixed-plant identifiers, submeter-to-equipment associations and zone-level presence checks that do not inspect device or research content. Coverage/timing: All declared asset classes and accessible locations; owner-approved snapshots at declaration, after moves or disposals, and at least quarterly, with scan time retained. Quality gate: verify ID-to-asset and reader-to-zone maps, scan and aggregation rules, functional checks, clock offset, uptime, failed or duplicate reads, mapping drift and lineage; physical calibration is not applicable. Report counts and owner-supplied value bands by zone; moved, duplicated, untagged, inaccessible or powered-off assets can remain unmatched and a detected tag does not prove ownership or condition.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: The insured-risk schedule custodian, estates asset owner, finance fixed-asset owner, IT or laboratory custodians and competent valuers. Policy schedules lead for contractual declaration, competent valuations for stated value, and current endorsed registers for physical inventory. Permissions/provenance: Use purpose-limited joins with source/version identifiers and asset-zone mapping lineage; show every mismatch and route it to the relevant owner rather than silently selecting a record. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain register effective, telemetry observed and query retrieved times; treat location or inventory evidence outside the current declaration window as stale; show schedule, register and observation mismatches together.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: lookup + comparison + calculation. Interval/evidence gate: At declaration, material change and annual assessment; require one current schedule, owner-approved registers and at least 90% mapped coverage by declared value band. Method: Three-way exposure reconciliation and concentration profiling. Keyed joins, duplicate and orphan detection, zone totals and exception sampling against a physical survey. Uncertainty/safe failure: State mapped count, mapped value-band share and unmatched share; mark the answer unknown where more than 10% of a material value band is unmapped or valuation dates are unsuitable.
Answer_Boundary: The service must not infer ownership from proximity, value unrecorded property, set sums insured, decide insurability, pricing, coverage or claim treatment, or treat a tag response as proof of serviceability.

Question: Which spaces appear to differ from the current owner-approved use record, and what material change must be confirmed before the declared exposure can be relied on?
Notes: Enables the assessor to determine whether a competent reassessment, updated declaration, altered survey scope or temporary-control discussion is needed.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Anonymous doorway counts, room booking-state indicators, zone power demand and environmental patterns used only as change cues; no audio, video, identities, device content or research activity is inspected. Coverage/timing: Mapped rooms and shared areas; 15-minute readings aggregated daily over at least 28 days, plus owner-declared dates for moves, events and temporary occupation. Quality gate: validate each counter or presence point against short manual samples; retain entrance coverage, sampling and aggregation, functional checks, clock offset, uptime, occlusion gaps, count drift and raw-to-zone lineage. Similar uses can produce similar signatures, open-plan spillover can distort room evidence and uninstrumented rooms remain unobserved; report only pattern differences, not a new use classification.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: Space management, estates, health and safety, local room custodians, timetabling and event or project owners. Current approved space records and written temporary-use permissions lead; competent fire, safety or planning findings lead within their scope. Permissions/provenance: Use only authorised booking and aggregate access metadata with documented transformations; expose stale room records and route declared-versus-observed conflicts to the space owner. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain schedule effective, interval observed and query retrieved times; planned states expire at their stated end; observations outside the comparison window are stale, and material differences go to the responsible owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: observation + comparison + estimate. Interval/evidence gate: Monthly and after a move, project or unusual event; require a current room register, 20 valid comparable days and at least two independent zone-level signals for any indicated change. Method: Declared-use reconciliation with change-point screening. Compare owner-declared use periods with robust baselines, change-point tests and rule-based exceptions, then seek owner confirmation. Uncertainty/safe failure: Report observed coverage, effect size and a high/medium/low evidence grade; return 'use not established' when evidence is sparse, mixed or seasonally incomparable.
Answer_Boundary: The service must not identify occupants, infer teaching or research content, determine legal change of use, occupancy class or compliance, authorise occupation, or state that policy terms respond.

Question: For each material-risk zone, when is it normally occupied, lightly staffed or apparently unattended, and how reliable is that pattern?
Notes: Supports survey timing, after-hours control checks, response-planning discussions and evidence requests for zones that are frequently unattended.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Anonymous bidirectional counters at selected entrances, zone presence sensors, door-state counts and lighting or plug-load activity, fused without identities or route reconstruction. Coverage/timing: Principal entrances and nominated material-risk zones; five-minute observations aggregated to 30-minute states, with separate weekday, weekend, event and closure profiles. Quality gate: validate each counter or presence point against short manual samples; retain entrance coverage, sampling and aggregation, functional checks, clock offset, uptime, occlusion gaps, count drift and raw-to-zone lineage. Tailgating, held-open doors, cleaners, maintenance visits, sensor occlusion and partial entrance coverage can bias counts; absence of signal is never proof that nobody is present.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: Security, facilities duty management, space management, timetabling, event owners and authorised opening-hours custodians. Approved opening, event and closure records lead; security access records lead for recorded access events, while commissioned telemetry supports only observed zone conditions. Permissions/provenance: Use least-privilege, aggregated access data and suppress small groups; retain sensor-health and mapping lineage, and present unresolved schedule-versus-observation differences. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain schedule effective, interval observed and query retrieved times; planned states expire at their stated end; observations outside the comparison window are stale, and material differences go to the responsible owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: observation + estimate. Interval/evidence gate: Weekly profiling and event-specific assessment; require four representative weeks, at least 85% valid intervals and coverage of every entrance used in the estimate. Method: Multi-signal occupancy-state estimation and unattended-window detection. Calendar reconciliation followed by probabilistic state fusion, with cross-validation against manually confirmed sample periods. Uncertainty/safe failure: Publish false-empty and false-occupied estimates from validation samples and confidence by time band; default to 'presence unknown' whenever coverage or validation gates fail.
Answer_Boundary: The service must not identify or track people, infer lone-worker identity or behaviour, promise security response, authorise opening, or use an estimated unattended state as a factual attendance record.

Question: Where are high-value, irreplaceable or continuity-critical assets concentrated, and which single peril zone or shared dependency could affect several together?
Notes: Enables a focused physical survey, separation or protection discussion, asset-register correction and continuity assessment for concentrated exposures.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Owner-approved asset-zone mapping, local leak detection, temperature and humidity sensing, power-state telemetry and verified fire or drainage zone references; no content from protected equipment is collected. Coverage/timing: All owner-declared critical assets and the rooms, cabinets or plant areas containing them; condition data at one- to fifteen-minute intervals and location snapshots after every recorded move. Quality gate: verify ID-to-asset and reader-to-zone maps, scan and aggregation rules, functional checks, clock offset, uptime, failed or duplicate reads, mapping drift and lineage; physical calibration is not applicable. Location accuracy is limited by tag mapping, shared rooms and mobile assets; condition sensors observe only their commissioned area and cannot establish replacement value or criticality.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: Asset custodians, finance, estates, IT service owners, research or teaching service owners and business-continuity leads. Competent valuations and owner-approved criticality records lead, followed by current asset registers and verified location records; telemetry supports only the observed condition and period. Permissions/provenance: Restrict detailed locations for security-sensitive assets, retain source/version and zone lineage, and show conflicts between value, criticality and location records to their owners. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain register effective, telemetry observed and query retrieved times; treat location or inventory evidence outside the current declaration window as stale; show schedule, register and observation mismatches together.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: lookup + calculation + comparison. Interval/evidence gate: At least annually and after material moves; require current criticality and value bands, at least 90% mapped declared value, and verified hazard-zone boundaries for the peril being considered. Method: Spatial accumulation and common-cause exposure analysis. Aggregate by room, compartment, drainage catchment, power source and environmental-control dependency, then test single-zone and single-service loss scenarios. Uncertainty/safe failure: Report exposed value and criticality as ranges with unmapped shares; do not rank zones when more than 15% of the relevant value or dependency mapping is uncertain.
Answer_Boundary: The service must not calculate or present a probable maximum loss, invent values, reveal restricted asset locations, decide coverage or recommend a premium, or treat co-location as proof of common damage.

Question: Which recurring events or operating peaks temporarily increase occupancy, electrical demand, combustibles, deliveries or access pressure beyond the normal profile?
Notes: Helps scope pre-event checks, temporary protection, security staffing discussions, specialist attendance and post-event evidence requests.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Approved event and booking indicators, anonymous entrance counts, aggregate electrical demand, temporary distribution-board monitoring, door-cycle counts and owner-declared temporary-storage checks. Coverage/timing: Event spaces, access routes and affected service zones; five-minute signals aggregated by event phase, with setup, live, close-down and overnight periods retained separately. Quality gate: validate each counter or presence point against short manual samples; retain entrance coverage, sampling and aggregation, functional checks, clock offset, uptime, occlusion gaps, count drift and raw-to-zone lineage. Electrical demand does not identify equipment, counts may miss entrances and temporary combustibles usually require inspection; compare only events with similar duration, season and operating mode.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: Event owners, timetabling, estates operations, security, fire-safety and temporary-power or contractor coordinators. Approved event plans, occupancy limits, permits and competent findings lead; observed telemetry can test stated timing and aggregate loading only. Permissions/provenance: Use event identifiers rather than attendee identities, document source joins and exclude restricted details; show any plan-versus-observation exception to the event and control owners. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain schedule effective, interval observed and query retrieved times; planned states expire at their stated end; observations outside the comparison window are stale, and material differences go to the responsible owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: observation + comparison. Interval/evidence gate: Before high-consequence events and quarterly for recurring events; require an approved plan, mapped affected zones, healthy signals for at least 90% of event duration and three comparable events where trend claims are made. Method: Event-phase exposure profiling and peak exception detection. Normalise counts, demand and door cycles by event duration and area, compare percentiles with the approved plan and identify concurrent temporary controls or impairments. Uncertainty/safe failure: Show observed peak ranges and data loss; use a single-event statement only as a bounded observation and return 'not comparable' when event types or coverage differ materially.
Answer_Boundary: The service must not identify attendees, infer event content or behaviour, certify occupancy or fire load, approve an event, or decide whether the exposure is acceptable under policy terms.

Question: Which declared hazardous, temperature-sensitive, irreplaceable or theft-attractive materials are present, where are they stored, and is their required storage envelope evidenced?
Notes: Enables the assessor to request a competent inspection, clarify declared stock, assess protection dependencies and preserve evidence of environmental excursions.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Enclosure or room temperature and humidity, leak and water-on-floor sensors, door-state counts, local power availability and approved storage-alarm status; no chemical, specimen or research content is sensed. Coverage/timing: Only owner-nominated storage rooms, cabinets and supporting services; one- to five-minute readings with hourly summaries and immediate recording of threshold excursions or power loss. Quality gate: confirm representative siting, asset or zone mapping, units, traceable calibration or functional check, sampling and aggregation, clock offset, uptime, gaps, response lag, drift and raw-to-summary lineage. A room sensor may not represent cabinet conditions, door opening can cause short excursions and sensor drift can mimic change; unmonitored stores and unverified set-points remain unknown.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: Health and safety, hazardous-materials or biological-safety owners, local custodians, security, estates and the asset or collections owner. Current approved inventories, storage specifications, safety documentation and competent findings lead; telemetry supports the observed environment only. Permissions/provenance: Minimise or withhold sensitive material identities and exact locations, use coded storage references, retain calibration and mapping provenance, and route conflicts to the competent owner. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain register effective, telemetry observed and query retrieved times; treat location or inventory evidence outside the current declaration window as stale; show schedule, register and observation mismatches together.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: lookup + observation + comparison. Interval/evidence gate: Daily for critical stores and after alarms or moves; require a current owner-approved requirement, verified sensor location, seven valid days for baseline claims and at least 95% interval completeness. Method: Storage-declaration reconciliation and environmental-envelope assessment. Compare measurements with the specified envelope using excursion duration, degree-time and service-state context rather than isolated threshold crossings. Uncertainty/safe failure: Report sensor uncertainty, coverage and excursion ranges; mark the condition unknown when cabinet representativeness, calibration or the authoritative requirement is unverified.
Answer_Boundary: The service must not disclose restricted inventories or exact locations, infer material identity, certify storage safety, determine regulatory compliance, control the store, or decide insurance response.

Question: What temporary exposure is created by active construction, refurbishment, commissioning, relocation or intrusive maintenance, and during which zones and time windows?
Notes: Supports targeted site attendance, evidence requests, temporary-protection discussion and confirmation that hand-back evidence is complete.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Approved permit-state feeds, temporary temperature, dust, water, differential-pressure or power monitoring, fire-system impairment indicators and door or barrier state at the defined work area. Coverage/timing: The mapped work zone, adjacent affected compartments and services; one- to five-minute observations during work and aftercare, plus daily owner-confirmed start, stop and hand-back times. Quality gate: for every contributing stream, verify asset and location mapping, units, calibration or functional check, sampling and aggregation, clock offset, uptime, gaps, drift and source-to-result lineage; exclude any stream that fails its gate. Temporary sensors are easily moved or damaged, permit status does not prove field compliance and some hazards require physical observation; unmapped work or undocumented changes cannot be analysed reliably.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners/precedence: Project sponsor, principal contractor, permit issuer, estates, fire-safety, health and safety, security and affected local custodians. Signed permits, approved method statements, isolation schedules and competent site findings lead; telemetry can corroborate stated conditions only within its mapped area and time. Permissions/provenance: Access contractor and security details only for the stated purpose, retain permit/version and sensor-placement provenance, and expose disagreement between planned, observed and hand-back states. Time/staleness/conflicts: retain schedule effective, interval observed and query retrieved times; planned states expire at their stated end; observations outside the comparison window are stale, and material differences go to the responsible owner.
Analysis_Required: Operation type: lookup + observation + comparison. Interval/evidence gate: Before work, each shift and at hand-back; require a current permit or written scope, mapped affected systems, named control owners and healthy evidence covering at least 90% of the higher-risk window. Method: Time-bounded works exposure and control-overlap assessment. Construct a timeline of work phases, isolations, temporary controls, alarms and environmental excursions, then identify periods with missing or overlapping safeguards.
