Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: sensor and facilities owners; competent electrical or mechanical professionals where relevant; BMS owner; instrument steward; and data steward. Precedence: verified installation and competent-owner evidence outrank visual suspicion; a correlated service state is a candidate explanation, not proof of interference. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: installation and nearby-source records must be current for each tested interval. Conflict rule: preserve unresolved competing explanations and do not assign a fault category without competent confirmation.
Analysis_Required: Operation: comparison plus diagnosis of measurement quality. Decision interval: at commissioning, after relocation or enclosure change, and when a state-linked anomaly appears. Minimum evidence: at least two interference states, a reference or negative-control location, repeated transitions, stable clocks and enough samples to separate time trend from state. Method: use blocked experiments where permitted, negative controls, regression with interaction terms and before-after co-location; test residual structure. Uncertainty: report effect intervals, false-event rates and sensitivity to alternative interference covariates. Safe failure: relocate or shield the sensor, include a correction only after validation, restrict the affected state or exclude the device.
Answer_Boundary: Do not create unsafe test conditions, diagnose building equipment, assume correlation identifies the interference source, or correct data using an unvalidated relationship.

Question: After a sensor is moved, replaced, reconfigured or reassigned, can the time series remain comparable, and from which effective time?
Notes: Preserves honest longitudinal evidence and prevents maintenance or relocation from masquerading as a research finding.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use effective-dated asset mapping, old and new devices in a planned overlap, traceable co-location, configuration and firmware telemetry, and the raw series on both sides of the change. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover the old and new positions, served zones and any unchanged reference location; verify current room use and service mapping independently. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Collect at least 48 hours and preferably seven days of overlap under varied states; retain native values and calculate the same fixed aggregates before and after. Record-specific quality check: verify both calibrations, UTC alignment, equivalent cadence, uptime, gaps, drift, response time and complete relocation or replacement provenance. Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: sensor and asset owners; facilities and current space owners; platform administrator; maintenance or project owner; and data steward. Precedence: signed or owner-confirmed change times and physical mapping outrank first or last observed record; a reused device identifier does not prove continuity. The May 2021 floor plan may support historical orientation only; current owner records and competent confirmation govern current use, access, services, hazards and closures. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: change records and mappings must carry exact effective times and configurations. Conflict rule: split the identity or interval whenever overlap, mapping or configuration evidence conflicts.
Analysis_Required: Operation: comparison plus estimate. Decision interval: before the change where planned, immediately after, and before longitudinal analysis. Minimum evidence: effective change time, old-new overlap, common reference, calibration and configuration records, at least two operating states and prespecified equivalence limits. Method: test level, variance, response and state-dependent equivalence; estimate bridging uncertainty and compare segmented, adjusted and unadjusted trends. Uncertainty: report equivalence intervals, change-point uncertainty and the effect of any bridge on long-term estimates. Safe failure: treat the series as separate eras, restrict to post-change data or state that longitudinal continuity is unavailable.
Answer_Boundary: Do not splice series because identifiers match, infer room continuity from the historical plan, overwrite the change boundary, or apply an adjustment outside its documented overlap.

Question: How can device, gateway, BMS point, meter, room and asset identifiers be linked across time without assuming that names are unique or stable?
Notes: Creates stable, time-aware joins and prevents silent identity collisions from contaminating longitudinal analysis.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use commissioned asset registries, platform identifiers, gateway association records, meter hierarchies and targeted physical verification; no wireless tracking or person identifiers are needed. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover every source identifier used in the study and all effective-dated parent relationships, including reused names, replacements and many-to-many service zones. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Capture mapping snapshots at extraction and all owner-confirmed change events; preserve raw identifiers and create a study surrogate that never overwrites source identity. Record-specific quality check: verify physical mapping, commissioning, clocked effective dates, uptime and gap context, drift flags where measurements are linked, and complete mapping provenance. Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: asset, BMS, metering, sensor-platform and current space-data owners; project records owner; and study data steward. Precedence: current commissioned registries and physical verification outrank string similarity, network proximity and the May 2021 plan; source identifiers retain their owner-defined meaning. The May 2021 floor plan may support historical orientation only; current owner records and competent confirmation govern current use, access, services, hazards and closures. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Method: use design-stage restriction or matching, prespecified adjustment sets, flexible outcome models and negative controls; assess overlap and collider risk. Uncertainty: report residual imbalance, uncertainty, sensitivity to unmeasured confounding and how estimates change across defensible adjustment sets. Safe failure: make an association-only claim, narrow the population or state that confounding cannot be controlled.
Answer_Boundary: Do not add every available variable, adjust for mediators or colliders without justification, infer individual behaviour, or present an adjusted association as automatically causal.

Question: How could sensor availability, room selection, access restrictions or exclusion rules make the analysed sample unrepresentative?
Notes: Makes coverage bias visible and supports a choice between rebalancing collection and narrowing the population claim.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use coverage, health, permission and mapping metadata for both included and excluded devices, rooms and periods; no additional occupant sensing is needed. Spatial coverage and limits: Describe the full eligible building scope and all selected or unavailable units, including uninstrumented, inaccessible and low-uptime strata. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Create weekly inclusion and exposure summaries and preserve the exact reason and time each unit enters or leaves the sample. Record-specific quality check: verify mapping, calibration status, clocks, uptime, gaps, drift and provenance for selected and non-selected evidence so quality filters do not hide systematic exclusion. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: current space and facilities owners; sensor-platform and access owners; ethics and governance owners; principal investigator; and data steward. Precedence: the prespecified eligibility frame and current authoritative access status outrank the convenience sample that happens to be available. The May 2021 floor plan may support historical orientation only; current owner records and competent confirmation govern current use, access, services, hazards and closures. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: selection and permission states must be effective-dated throughout collection. Conflict rule: preserve denied, unhealthy and ambiguous units as named frame categories and do not silently remove them.
Analysis_Required: Operation: comparison plus estimate. Decision interval: at recruitment or site selection, monthly during collection and before population claims. Minimum evidence: a complete eligibility frame, inclusion probabilities or reasons, key structural variables for included and excluded units, and outcome-independent selection rules. Method: compare distributions, fit selection models or weights where support exists, and calculate worst-case bounds for missing strata. Uncertainty: report standardised differences, effective sample size after weighting and uncertainty under unobserved selection. Safe failure: limit inference to the observed sample, target a narrower population or collect evidence in underrepresented strata.
Answer_Boundary: Do not call a convenient instrumented sample representative, weight beyond common support, hide permission-related exclusions, or infer characteristics of unobserved rooms or users.

Question: How should an anomaly detector be evaluated when true faults or unusual events are rare, labels are imperfect and normal operation changes?
Notes: Shows whether the detector adds value beyond simple baselines and whether alert burden and uncertainty are acceptable for a bounded research deployment.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use the approved environmental, BMS, metering or platform-health streams plus owner-confirmed event records and deliberately constructed safe test cases; do not create hazardous conditions or infer personal behaviour. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover multiple verified assets, rooms and operating regimes, with separate training and future or asset-held-out evaluation periods. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Retain native event timing and predeclared feature windows; score continuously but aggregate alerts by a defined incident or episode rule. Record-specific quality check: verify mapping, calibration relevance, clock alignment, uptime, gaps, drift, label timing and model-input provenance. Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: facilities and competent technical owners; BMS or platform owners; maintenance event owner; model owner; principal investigator; and data steward. Precedence: competent-owner confirmation outranks model scores; absence of a logged fault is not proof that an alert is false, and an anomaly is not a fault label. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: label definitions and operating regimes must be effective for each event. Conflict rule: retain uncertain labels and score them separately rather than forcing binary truth.
Analysis_Required: Operation: forecast plus comparison; no operational diagnosis. Decision interval: during model development, before deployment and after regime or sensor change. Minimum evidence: an untouched time-or asset-held-out set, at least 30 confirmed events or a justified rare-event design, realistic normal exposure, defined alert burden and label uncertainty. Method: compare simple statistical and persistence baselines with the proposed model; use event-level precision, recall, time-to-detection, false alerts per asset-day and calibration. Uncertainty: report 95% intervals, prevalence sensitivity, performance by regime and degradation under label, drift and missing-data uncertainty. Safe failure: keep the model exploratory, require human triage, collect labels or decline fault-detection claims.
Answer_Boundary: Do not treat an anomaly score as a confirmed fault, optimise only for overall accuracy, use post-event information at prediction time or deploy alerts from a model whose false-alarm burden and drift response are unknown.

Question: Across which seasons, timetable regimes and operational states does a forecast remain calibrated, and how far ahead is it useful?
Notes: Identifies the horizons and regimes where forecasting improves decisions and where a simple baseline or no forecast is safer.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use approved historical and near-real-time outcome streams with only covariates available by forecast issue time, such as published weather forecasts, calendar features and known control schedules. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover the verified target rooms or systems and hold out complete future periods and, where possible, unseen units. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Retain native data, define issue time and horizon, and create fixed training, validation and rolling test origins; prevent late-arriving or future data from entering features. Record-specific quality check: verify mapping, calibration continuity, clocks, source latency, uptime, gaps, drift and feature-availability provenance at each forecast origin. Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: source-system, weather, timetable, facilities and sensor owners; model owner; principal investigator; and data steward. Precedence: data actually available at issue time outrank retrospectively complete stores; current operating state and owner-confirmed changes outrank historical regularity. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: forecast inputs, mappings and schedules must be valid at every origin. Conflict rule: mark origins with unavailable or conflicting inputs as no-forecast rather than backfilling them with later knowledge.
Analysis_Required: Operation: forecast plus comparison. Decision interval: at each candidate horizon, before deployment and at monthly recalibration checks. Minimum evidence: at least one full seasonal cycle where seasonality is claimed or a narrower scope, rolling origins, a naive persistence and seasonal baseline, and enough events for calibration assessment. Method: use blocked rolling evaluation, probabilistic forecasts, calibration curves, proper scoring rules and performance by regime and horizon. Uncertainty: report prediction intervals, coverage, sharpness, calibration error, gain over the baseline and uncertainty under drift and missing inputs. Safe failure: issue no forecast, shorten the horizon, revert to the baseline or restrict to supported regimes.
Answer_Boundary: Do not use future information, present point predictions without uncertainty, promise accuracy after unobserved operational change, or let forecasts control systems without separate authority.

Question: What assumptions are needed for a causal interpretation, which can be strengthened by design, and which remain untestable?
Notes: Makes the causal claim conditional and testable and helps the team decide whether stronger design, narrower wording or a different question is needed.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use only evidence needed for exposure, outcome, measured common causes, timing and intervention assignment; add no intrusive sensing merely to make a causal claim possible. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover treated and comparison units, relevant shared systems and the full pre and post intervals with stable measurement. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Retain event and observation times at native precision, lock the temporal order and define exposure windows before outcome inspection. Record-specific quality check: verify mapping, calibration, clock alignment, uptime, gaps, drift and provenance equally across exposure groups. Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: principal investigator; subject-matter and method experts; operational change owner; facilities and source owners; ethics and governance owners; and data steward. Precedence: documented intervention assignment and current operational facts outrank analyst inference; statistical adjustment cannot replace unmeasured design information. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: assumptions and source meanings must match the exact study period and target population. Conflict rule: retain competing causal structures and downgrade the claim when they imply materially different estimates.
Analysis_Required: Operation: estimate with causal interpretation only under an explicit identification strategy. Decision interval: before data inspection, after design diagnostics and before claim wording. Minimum evidence: a causal graph, temporal ordering, positivity, stable measurement, no material interference beyond the defined unit, a justified comparison and prespecified falsification tests. Method: prefer randomisation or phased assignment where feasible; otherwise use natural experiments, difference-in-differences, instrumental variables or adjustment only when assumptions fit the setting. Uncertainty: report assumption-specific estimates, 95% intervals, placebo and negative-control results and sensitivity to hidden bias. Safe failure: state an association, present multiple bounded explanations or declare the causal question unanswered.
Answer_Boundary: Do not present model adjustment as proof of causation, claim that measured covariates remove unmeasured confounding or use causal language when exposure timing, interference or counterfactual assumptions are unsupported.

Question: Which robustness checks, negative controls and alternative specifications could reveal dependence on one fragile analytical choice?
Notes: Shows whether the conclusion is stable enough to act on and identifies the exact modelling choice that needs stronger evidence.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use the same verified study evidence plus prespecified negative-control variables, periods or units that should not respond under the proposed explanation; do not add arbitrary variables after seeing results. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover the complete primary sample and matched controls, with identical spatial and temporal inclusion rules. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Retain native data and generate a finite locked set of alternative windows, aggregations, exclusions and models; log every executed specification. Record-specific quality check: verify calibration, clocks, uptime, gaps, drift and provenance once and propagate identical quality rules across all specifications. Evidence gate: confirm modality, position, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, permission, calibration or reference evidence, UTC offset, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift, and device, firmware, configuration and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine failed intervals.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: principal investigator; method lead; source owners; subject-matter expert; and data steward. Precedence: the prespecified robustness plan outranks post-result experimentation; negative controls require a defensible reason, not merely a null expectation. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: specifications must be frozen before headline interpretation and linked to the same dataset version. Conflict rule: show all planned results, including contradictory ones, and do not discard a check because it weakens the narrative.
Analysis_Required: Operation: comparison plus estimate. Decision interval: after the primary model is locked and before publication or operational communication. Minimum evidence: a primary specification, at least three substantively plausible alternatives, one or more negative controls where valid, identical data quality gates and a defined robustness criterion. Method: use specification curves, multiverse summaries, placebo dates or locations, leave-one-unit-out analysis and alternative missingness treatments. Uncertainty: report the distribution of estimates, sign and decision stability, control results and uncertainty without counting correlated specifications as independent evidence. Safe failure: downgrade the claim, identify the fragile assumption or report the result as unresolved.
Answer_Boundary: Do not search unlimited specifications, report only favourable checks, treat a failed negative control as irrelevant, or convert robustness frequency into a probability that the claim is true.

Question: How should measurement error, sampling variation, missingness, model choice and transfer uncertainty be combined for the intended decision?
Notes: Connects statistical uncertainty to a real choice and shows whether the next best action is adoption, a limited pilot, more evidence or no change.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use calibrated measurement uncertainty, coverage and gap evidence, repeated samples across independent units, model outputs and target-context metadata; no additional sensing is justified unless one component dominates the decision. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover every evidence source contributing to the decision and the target units or contexts to which the recommendation may apply. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Calculate uncertainty at the declared decision interval and preserve component-specific inputs rather than collapsing quality into one score. Record-specific quality check: verify calibration and placement evidence, clocks, uptime, gaps, drift and provenance for every component before propagation. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: instrument and source owners; method lead; principal investigator; target decision owner; information governance where risk matters; and data steward. Precedence: owner-defined operational consequences and current evidence limits outrank a generic confidence threshold; competent professionals retain authority for safety and compliance decisions. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: loss, threshold and target-context assumptions must be current at the decision date. Conflict rule: present conflicting loss functions or thresholds separately and do not average away an owner disagreement.
Analysis_Required: Operation: calculation plus recommendation. Decision interval: at each major decision point and before communicating a recommended action. Minimum evidence: component uncertainty estimates, dependence assumptions, plausible model set, missingness scenarios, target-context overlap and an explicit consequence or loss table. Method: propagate uncertainty by simulation or Bayesian modelling, decompose variance where possible and perform decision or value-of-information analysis. Uncertainty: report total and component intervals, probability of crossing the decision threshold, expected regret and sensitivity to loss and transfer assumptions. Safe failure: recommend more evidence, a reversible pilot, no action or an explicitly cautious descriptive conclusion.
Answer_Boundary: Do not hide uncertainty in a traffic-light label, promise certainty, certify safety or compliance, or recommend operational control outside the responsible owner's authority.

Question: What is the minimum data content, granularity and retention period that can answer the approved question?
Notes: Creates a defensible data specification that reduces exposure, cost and governance burden without sacrificing the approved question.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use no person-identifying modality by default. Prefer room or system environmental telemetry, coarse anonymous counts and owner-held operational data, with fields and resolution limited to the stated estimand. Spatial coverage and limits: Restrict coverage to approved locations and periods; exclude sensitive rooms, identifiers and fine spatial traces unless separately justified and authorised. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Collect at the coarsest cadence that preserves the target signal, aggregate early where defensible and set deletion or irreversible reduction dates before collection. Record-specific quality check: verify source mapping and health, retain only clock, gap, drift and calibration metadata necessary for quality, and preserve provenance without exposing sensitive operational detail. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: principal investigator; data owners; information governance and security teams; ethics approval holder; records owner; and data steward. Precedence: approved purpose, minimisation and retention controls outrank analytical convenience; source owners may impose stricter limits. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: permissions and retention dates must be current and tied to the exact data specification. Conflict rule: adopt the stricter rule when approvals conflict and exclude data that cannot be justified field by field.
Analysis_Required: Operation: recommendation plus comparison. Decision interval: before collection, before linkage and at each retention checkpoint. Minimum evidence: a field-to-estimand justification, candidate resolutions, utility test, disclosure-risk assessment, storage and retention plan and deletion verification method. Method: compare analytical utility and risk across reduced datasets; test whether each field or resolution materially changes the prespecified result. Uncertainty: report utility loss intervals, residual risk and which conclusions become unsupported after minimisation. Safe failure: remove the field, aggregate further, shorten retention or decline the research question.
Answer_Boundary: Do not collect data for unspecified future use, retain maximum resolution by default, infer sensitive traits, or claim that de-identification eliminates all risk.

Question: Which ethics, governance, data-owner and security approvals must be in force before collection, linkage, analysis or sharing begins?
Notes: Gives the team a clear lawful and institutional route before real evidence is collected or linked.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: No sensing or extraction should begin for this question. Use a proposed data-flow diagram, modality and location specification, sample schema, access model and security-control evidence. Spatial coverage and limits: Describe every proposed source, location, recipient, linkage, environment and output route, including external collaborators and cloud services. Temporal coverage and aggregation: State collection cadence, aggregation, retention, refresh and deletion in the submission; do not test with real data before the relevant permissions exist. Record-specific quality check: include planned calibration, clock, uptime, gap, drift and provenance controls so approvals cover the actual evidence design rather than a vague sensor label. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: institutional ethics body; data and asset owners; information governance and security teams; facilities and safety owners; principal investigator; sponsor and data steward. Precedence: formal approvals and owner permissions outrank technical feasibility, informal agreement or prior project precedent. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: each approval must be current, purpose-specific, effective-dated and linked to the final data-flow specification. Conflict rule: stop the affected activity when requirements conflict and obtain a documented decision from the competent authority.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup plus recommendation. Decision interval: at concept design, before any pilot, and after material change in modality, linkage, purpose, recipient or risk. Minimum evidence: a complete data-flow and responsibility matrix, data classification, lawful or institutional basis, risk controls, participant route where applicable, retention, incident and sharing arrangements. Method: map every activity to required authority and evidence; test the proposed design against data minimisation, separation of duties and least privilege. Uncertainty: report unresolved requirements, dependencies and residual risk rather than a single approval label. Safe failure: redesign, defer or cancel the activity; use synthetic fixtures until permissions are complete.
Answer_Boundary: Do not begin collection or linkage because data are technically reachable, treat ethics approval as owner permission, or extend one approved purpose, population, modality, location or retention period to another without authority.

Question: When are participant information, consent or an opt-out route required, and how will participation remain genuinely voluntary?
Notes: Protects participants and gives the research team a credible way to collect only what people were accurately told and permitted.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Prefer non-identifying room or system measures. Where participants are directly involved, use only the approved modality and visible study devices; avoid covert imaging, audio, wireless-device capture and biometric inference. Spatial coverage and limits: Limit collection to declared locations, populations and periods, with practical non-participation zones or alternative arrangements where the protocol requires them. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Run only during approved windows, display current notices and apply consent or opt-out state before collection or inclusion; aggregate as early as possible. Record-specific quality check: verify device mapping, calibration, clock alignment, uptime, gaps, drift and consent-state provenance without storing unnecessary identity links. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: ethics approval holder; principal investigator; institutional governance; building and space owners; participant-facing study team; and data steward. Precedence: the approved participant route and current notice or consent materials outrank researcher assumption; employment or study relationships require careful power assessment. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: materials and consent state must be valid at the time of collection and after protocol amendments. Conflict rule: exclude affected data when consent or notice evidence is missing, disputed or technically unenforceable.
Analysis_Required: Operation: lookup plus observation. Decision interval: before recruitment or collection and continuously during participant-facing activity. Minimum evidence: approved information and consent route, versioned notices, eligibility and withdrawal rules, technical enforcement tests and a record of coverage without unnecessary personal detail. Method: trace each collected record class to the applicable participant basis, test opt-out exclusions and assess whether non-participation is practical and non-penalising. Uncertainty: report notice reach limits, consent-state uncertainty and any sample bias introduced by opt-out or non-participation. Safe failure: pause collection, remove affected records or redesign to use non-participant aggregate evidence.
Answer_Boundary: Do not imply mandatory participation, conceal sensor capabilities, use consent for a different purpose, or identify people to enforce an aggregate research design.

Question: Could repeated room-level aggregates enable re-identification or reconstruction of individual routines when linked with external knowledge?
Notes: Prevents apparently harmless aggregates from becoming a longitudinal record of identifiable routines.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use the proposed aggregate dataset, release schedule and plausible auxiliary information; no new sensing is required to test disclosure risk. Spatial coverage and limits: Assess all rooms, time windows and rare operating periods, especially small groups, unusual schedules and stable repeated patterns. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Evaluate the exact proposed cadence, history length and update frequency; include cumulative risk from repeated releases, not only one snapshot. Record-specific quality check: verify spatial mapping and timestamp precision, source uptime and gaps, drift and provenance because irregular coverage can itself reveal routines. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: information governance and security teams; data owners; ethics approval holder; principal investigator; disclosure-control specialist; and data steward. Precedence: approved risk appetite and realistic attacker knowledge outrank claims that data are anonymous because names were removed. The May 2021 floor plan may support historical orientation only; current owner records and competent confirmation govern current use, access, services, hazards and closures. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: risk must be reassessed for each release, recipient, linkage context and cumulative history. Conflict rule: apply the stricter control when utility and disclosure assessments disagree or attacker knowledge is uncertain.
Analysis_Required: Operation: diagnosis of disclosure risk plus recommendation. Decision interval: before any sharing or dashboard release and after each material update. Minimum evidence: the exact proposed dataset, recipient and access model, plausible auxiliary data, repeated-release history, small-cell distribution and a defined acceptable-risk threshold. Method: conduct motivated-intruder scenarios, uniqueness and linkage analysis, differencing attacks and membership or attribute-inference tests where applicable. Uncertainty: report risk ranges, vulnerable strata, assumptions about attacker knowledge and residual risk after controls. Safe failure: aggregate further, delay or batch releases, suppress vulnerable cells, restrict access or withhold the dataset.
Answer_Boundary: Do not claim that aggregation guarantees anonymity, publish fine-grained occupancy-like traces, test re-identification using unauthorised external data or disclose a plausible individual routine.

Question: How should small cells, rare events and extremes be protected without erasing the scientifically important pattern?
Notes: Preserves valuable rare-event evidence where possible while preventing outputs from exposing individuals or sensitive operations.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use the exact proposed table, figure or query output and its contributing counts, duration and uncertainty; no additional physical sensing is needed. Spatial coverage and limits: Cover every room, period, subgroup and event category in the output, including combinations created by filters or drill-down. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Assess both single and repeated releases at the declared aggregation interval; preserve suppressed values in the secure environment only when permitted. Record-specific quality check: verify mapping and time granularity, source uptime and gaps, drift flags and output lineage so suppressed and unsuppressed cells are reproducible. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: data owners; information governance; ethics approval holder; disclosure-control specialist; principal investigator; and data steward. Precedence: approved disclosure thresholds and contextual risk outrank a generic minimum count; rare operational events may also reveal sensitive building information. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: rules must be current for each recipient and release route. Conflict rule: use the more protective rule when count, duration, uniqueness or differencing risks conflict.
Analysis_Required: Operation: calculation plus recommendation. Decision interval: before every external output and interactive dashboard configuration. Minimum evidence: cell counts and exposure, secondary-disclosure paths, repeated-release history, plausible auxiliary knowledge, scientific utility target and approved risk threshold. Method: apply primary and complementary suppression, category combination, interval reporting, noise or controlled query budgets as appropriate; test differencing attacks. Uncertainty: report utility loss, residual disclosure risk and the number and type of protected cells without revealing their values. Safe failure: release a coarser summary, controlled-access output or no result for the vulnerable stratum.
Answer_Boundary: Do not reveal suppressed values through totals, filters or error bars, equate rarity with error, or remove important extremes without declaring the resulting scope limit.

Question: What additional privacy or security risk is created by linking two otherwise acceptable datasets, and is the linkage still proportionate?
Notes: Shows whether the scientific gain from linkage justifies the new risk and which architecture keeps that risk proportionate.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Use metadata and safe samples from the exact proposed sources, join keys, time and spatial resolution, recipient and output; do not perform the real linkage before approval. Spatial coverage and limits: Limit the assessment to approved locations and periods and identify whether combined data reveal routines, sensitive assets or operational dependencies absent from either source alone. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Model the declared linkage frequency, history length and refresh; include failed and ambiguous joins because they affect both privacy and scientific validity. Record-specific quality check: verify identifier semantics, clock alignment, uptime, gaps, drift flags and provenance needed for the join without expanding identity content. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: owners of every source; information governance and security teams; ethics approval holder; principal investigator; and data steward. Precedence: the combined-data risk classification and most restrictive source terms outrank the classification of each dataset alone. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: permissions must explicitly cover linkage purpose, keys, recipients, resolution, retention and outputs. Conflict rule: do not link when owner terms conflict; redesign with safer keys or a trusted linkage environment.
Analysis_Required: Operation: diagnosis of linkage risk plus recommendation. Decision interval: before linkage, after any added source or resolution change, and before sharing linked outputs. Minimum evidence: complete data-flow, join-key analysis, uniqueness and small-cell distribution, attacker model, source terms, linkage accuracy target and mitigation options. Method: compare unlinked and linked identifiability, attribute inference, operational sensitivity and join error; assess trusted-third-party, pseudonymous and aggregate alternatives. Uncertainty: report incremental risk, linkage-error intervals, vulnerable combinations and residual risk after controls. Safe failure: do not link, use coarser or one-time linkage, keep analysis inside a trusted environment or release only aggregate results.
Answer_Boundary: Do not assume two low-risk datasets remain low risk when combined, use personal identifiers for convenience, or let a technically successful join override source permissions.

Question: Are images, intelligible audio, wireless-device signals or other high-risk modalities necessary, or can lower-risk evidence answer the question?
Notes: Forces a necessity test before high-risk sensing and usually directs the study toward simpler, more proportionate evidence.
Sensors_Required: Proposed evidence: Default to no collection of identifiable images, intelligible audio, MAC addresses, device fingerprints or biometric signals. Compare safer alternatives such as non-recording sound level, low-resolution thermal count without storage, doorway beam counts or room-system telemetry. Spatial coverage and limits: Any exceptional modality must be confined to approved locations, fields of view or radio scope, exclude adjacent spaces and have visible safeguards and immediate reduction where feasible. Temporal coverage and aggregation: Collect only during approved windows at the minimum cadence and retention; disable raw capture when derived anonymous counts meet the purpose. Record-specific quality check: verify physical masking, calibration, clock alignment, uptime, gaps, drift, edge-reduction behaviour and secure provenance; independently test that raw high-risk content is not retained. Evidence gate: for physical inputs, carry forward verified modality and location, asset/zone mapping, commissioning, calibration or reference evidence, UTC alignment, cadence, uptime, gaps and backfill or resampling, drift and device, firmware and configuration lineage. For artefacts, retain schema, version, hash and raw-to-derived lineage; quarantine unresolved failures.
Authoritative_Sources: Owners and authority: ethics body; information governance and security teams; building and space owners; competent safety owner; modality specialist; principal investigator; and data steward. Precedence: formal necessity and proportionality approval outrank technical availability; any bystander, neighbouring-space or wireless scope restriction is authoritative. Time, permission and lineage: retain valid-from, observation or event, ingestion and retrieval times; record purpose and permission scope, owner, source version or hash, extraction identifier and transformations. Currency rule: approval, signage, masking and retention must be current throughout collection. Conflict rule: stop collection immediately when masking, scope, notice, storage or deletion controls disagree or fail.
Analysis_Required: Operation: comparison plus recommendation. Decision interval: before procurement or deployment and after any capability or location change. Minimum evidence: a precise estimand, alternatives table, utility evidence, privacy and security threat model, technical safeguard tests, retention and deletion plan and explicit authority. Method: compare scientific utility, error, operational burden and residual risk of each modality; test raw-data leakage and adversarial reconstruction of derived outputs.
